detail.abstract: This qualitative study investigates the administrative barriers, system-readiness conditions, and fraudprevention realities of deploying distributed ledger technology (DLT) for bank reconciliation within hotel accounting ecosystems. While the technical promise of blockchain-based reconciliation immutable records, continuous matching, and cryptographic audit trails is widely asserted, the organizational realities of its deployment in the hospitality sector remain poorly understood. Grounded in the internal-control framework and routinization perspectives on technology adoption, this research adopts an exploratory multi-case design encompassing semi-structured interviews with finance directors, internal auditors, IT leaders, and external advisors across hotel operators at varying stages of DLT adoption, triangulated with documentary evidence. Thematic analysis surfaced two conditioning themes administrative barriers and system readiness a core reconciliation mechanism, and two outcome themes capturing fraud and embezzlement mitigation and revenue security through cash-leakage control. The findings reveal that automated, real-time reconciliation reduces the manual touchpoints through which asset misappropriation and cash leakage typically occur, shortens detection latency, and strengthens segregation of duties, while its efficacy is strongly conditioned by data-integration maturity, banking-API connectivity, and the resolution of governance and regulatory ambiguity. The study contributes an empirically grounded account of DLTenabled internal control and offers actionable guidance for hospitality finance leaders.

title: A comprehensive review of neural network--based approaches for retinal blood vessel segmentation in fundus images
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Ostrava - University Hospital Ostrava and University of Ostrava - University Hospital Ostrava

detail.title: A comprehensive review of neural network--based approaches for retinal blood vessel segmentation in fundus images
detail.abstract: Automated analysis of retinal fundus images, particularly blood vessel segmentation, is essential for diagnosing and monitoring ocular and systemic diseases. Over the past decade, neural network-based methods for retinal vessel segmentation have grown rapidly, yet challenges remain in reproducibility, clinical validation, and generalizability. This systematic review, conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines, synthesizes retinal vessel segmentation research published between 2016 and 2025. We analyzed 198 studies selected from 4,753 records identified through Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and PubMed. The review provides a comprehensive overview of methodological trends, dataset usage, and evaluation practices. It summarizes architectural evolution from convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to Transformers and generative adversarial networks (GANs), as well as preprocessing, augmentation, training configurations, loss functions, postprocessing methods, evaluation metrics, and reproducibility practices. Our analysis shows that CNN-based methods, particularly U-Net variants, remain the dominant approach. Although benchmark performance appears saturated, results are supported by heterogeneous and often underreported methodological choices. Important gaps persist: cross-dataset validation is inconsistent, public code availability remains limited, and statistical uncertainty is rarely reported. In addition, the heavy reliance on a small number of datasets containing predominantly healthy subjects raises concerns regarding bias and generalizability to pathological conditions. This review identifies fragmented evaluation and limited transparency as major barriers to clinical translation. By mapping methodological trends and architectural developments, we provide recommendations for standardized evaluation, diversified validation, and open-science practices to support future progress in retinal vessel segmentation research.

detail.abstract: This study examines how inflationary macroeconomic shocks erode the efficacy of classical working capital metrics in emerging-market service firms, and whether the relationship between aggressive inventory and receivable management and corporate liquidity survival is non-linear. Grounded in the trade-off theory of working capital and the precautionary-liquidity perspective, we theorize that inflation shocks compress working capital efficiency, that aggressive working capital maneuvering exhibits an inverted U relationship with liquidity survival, and that inflation moderates the inventory receivable liquidity nexus. Drawing on an unbalanced panel of 318 listed service firms across several emerging economies over the period 2008 2023 (4,214 firm-year observations), we employ a dynamic panel estimator the two step System Generalized Method of Moments (System GMM) to address the persistence of liquidity, unobserved heterogeneity, and the endogeneity of working capital policy. The results confirm a significant negative effect of inflation shocks on working capital efficiency, a significant inverted-U relationship between working capital aggressiveness and liquidity survival (turning point identified), and a significant moderating role of inflation that shifts the optimum toward more conservative policy. Diagnostic tests (AR(2), Hansen) support the validity of the specification. The study advances working capital theory in high-inflation regimes and offers actionable guidance for treasury and finance executives in emerging markets.

title: On the Feasibility of a Free Trade Agreement between Cambodia and Mongolia

detail.title: On the Feasibility of a Free Trade Agreement between Cambodia and Mongolia
detail.abstract: This paper examines the feasibility of an FTA between Kingdom of Cambodia and Mongolia in light of increasing economic collaboration among South East Asian (ASIAN) and Northeast Asian countries, with a particular emphasis on increased trade volumes of both countries with China. Under the most favourable situation, Mongolia's exports to Cambodia will increase by 124.6%, and its import from Cambodia by 237.0% after 12 years of signing an FTA. These are equivalent to 0.05% and 0.031% of Mongolia's GDP for 2019. Mongolia's current policy stance indicates Mongolia would be keen to establish an FTA with Cambodia. Although the estimated amount of trade creation and export diversifying effects could be minimal, the main benefit would be to signal others that Mongolia is interested in establishing bilateral agreements. Moreover, a Cambodia-Mongolia FTA could potentially complement the recently signed Cambodia-China FTA and enhance Mongolia's trade relationship with China.

title: Constitutional Architecture as Military Advantage in the Battlefield - The Reliability Dividend (LAWS Series, paper 3)

detail.title: Constitutional Architecture as Military Advantage in the Battlefield - The Reliability Dividend (LAWS Series, paper 3)
detail.abstract: The debate over lethal autonomous weapons systems (LAWS) has been structured, almost without exception, by an assumed trade-off: constitutional constraint on autonomous lethal action is ethically demanded but militarily costly. The state that binds its weapons pays in operational effectiveness what it earns in normative standing. This paper (the third and final in a series developing a structural sovereignty framework for LAWS governance) argues that the trade-off is illusory under realistic conditions of modern combat, and that its inversion carries significant consequences for both military doctrine and international governance. The central claim is architectural: the same constitutional mechanisms that prevent what we defined as "monotonic normative drift" and preserve human sovereignty under electronic warfare-hardware-externalized authorization (ATC-M), time-locked mandates, isolated telemetry enclaves, and monotonic authority contraction (Constitutional Compression)-are also the mechanisms that keep an autonomous weapon epistemically reliable when the battlefield degrades. Four reliability dividends are developed: structural resistance to electronic capture; prevention of algorithmic fratricide; command predictability under communications denial; and the preservation of command responsibility when the authorization chain can no longer be exercised in real time. The argument displaces the question that has organized the LAWS literature. Under this framework the question is no longer only "how do we prevent unlawful killings?" but "how do we keep autonomous weapons epistemically reliable under battlefield degradation?" and the answer to the second question turns out to satisfy the first. The paper concludes with the governance implication: a constraint architecture that functions as a reliability multiplier converts LAWS regulation from a collective-action problem into an incentive-compatible standard.

title:
Does News Sentiment Precede Liquidity Shocks? 
A Liquidity-first Event Study of Indian Equities

detail.title:
Does News Sentiment Precede Liquidity Shocks? 
A Liquidity-first Event Study of Indian Equities

declarations.declarationOfInterest: "The author declares no conflicts of interest."
declarations.funderStatement: "This research received no external funding. It was conducted as part of a Professional Doctorate in Data Science at the University of East London."

detail.abstract: This study examines whether abnormal public-news sentiment precedes firm-level liquidity shocks in Indian equities using a liquidity-first event design. The sample contains 74 event observations across 69 NSE-listed companies between 2022 and 2025, with 90.5% concentrated in 2024-2025. Relative to event-specific pre-event baselines and historical pseudo-events, broad entityconditioned GDELT tone shows abnormal absolute sentiment displacement at T-1 (1.506 versus a historical null mean of 1.123; raw p = 0.035). The result is suggestive after Holm correction across the pre-specified T-1/T0 family (p = 0.070) and is directionally consistent across pre-specified and algorithmically discovered events. Liquidity-event dates exhibit unusually large absolute price movements without corresponding increases in trading volume, consistent with elevated price impact. More restrictive headlineexplicit GDELT and entity-conditioned LLM sentiment do not show equivalent abnormal displacement, indicating that the lead signal is strongest in the wider company-associated information environment. The findings provide period-specific evidence that broad news sentiment can precede identified liquidity shocks, while whether this relationship persists across materially different macro-financial regimes remains an empirical question.

title: Managing Uncertainty in Oncology Drug Approvals in China
affiliations: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College (CAMS & PUMC) - Clinical Trial Center, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College (CAMS & PUMC) - Clinical Trial Center, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College (CAMS & PUMC) - Department of Radiation Oncology, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College (CAMS & PUMC) - Clinical Trial Center and Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College (CAMS & PUMC) - Clinical Trial Center

detail.title: Managing Uncertainty in Oncology Drug Approvals in China
detail.abstract:
Background: Expedited approval pathways and single-arm design have been frequently used in oncology approvals worldwide including in China. To inform future lifecycle regulatory improvement, we aimed to characterize the approval-time evidence gaps of recent oncology drug approvals in China and to examine how these gaps may be managed through post-marketing regulatory oversight.

Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional study of oncology drug approvals granted by China’s National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) between Jan 1, 2023, and Dec 31, 2025. For each indication, we extracted approval-time characteristics of the pivotal trial or trials, including trial design, efficacy, safety, and population representativeness. We mapped these data to 10 prespecified binary evidence-gap indicators, representing unresolved evidence questions at approval across domains commonly considered in regulatory and health technology assessments. We summarized the frequency and clustering of these indicators overall and by approval pathway. We also compared post-marketing regulatory mechanisms relevant to addressing these gaps across China, the United States, Europe and Japan.

Findings: A total of 177 approved indications were identified. 173 (97.7%) indications had at least one evidence gap, and 91 (51.4%) had four or more. The most common gaps were the non-inclusion of patients with an ECOG performance status of 2 or higher (77.4%) or patients aged 75 years or older (38.4%), and OS evidence that was either unreported or showed unfavorable trend (32.8%). Compared with regular approvals, conditional approvals more often lacked a concurrent comparator (89·8% vs 12.7%), used response-based primary endpoints without mature survival evidence (94·9% vs 14·4%), and had safety populations of 100 patients or fewer (32·2% vs 8·5%). Conversely, no substantial clinical benefit and treatment-related discontinuation rates of at least 20% were more frequent among regular approvals (22·0% vs 16·9% and 13·6% vs 3·4%, respectively). OS-related and population-representativeness gaps remained common in both pathways. All four agencies had formal post-marketing mechanisms relevant to addressing these gaps, but differed in the transparency and intensity of ongoing oversight.

Interpretation: Approval-time evidence gaps were common among recent oncology approvals in China, particularly regarding the representation of older and functionally impaired patients and the maturity of long-term efficacy evidence. These findings reflect a challenge in balancing earlier patient access with the need for sufficiently mature evidence. China has established a post-marketing regulatory framework broadly aligned with those of other major regulators. Continued refinement of indication-specific evidence generation, transparent progress tracking, and timely reassessment could further strengthen lifecycle regulation and support durable patient benefit.

title: The €82 Million That Never Existed: Anatomy of a Citation Chain, from NATO 2014 to an AI Research Report — and Who Is Actually Cognitively Vulnerable

detail.title: The €82 Million That Never Existed: Anatomy of a Citation Chain, from NATO 2014 to an AI Research Report — and Who Is Actually Cognitively Vulnerable

detail.abstract: In 2016 a European think tank attributed to Russia an €82 million investment in NGOs opposing shale gas. The only source was an anonymous interview. This paper traces the claim's twelve-year citation chain and shows that it split in June 2014 into two branches with opposite fates: an English-language branch that gained a number and shed a caution at every hop (Hudson/Washington Examiner, Martens Centre 2016, The Hill 2022), and an Italian branch that entered the country once — Corriere della Sera, December 2, 2014 — in the conditional mood, with the denial printed alongside and no figures at all. Systematic searches of the Corriere historical archive, the Italian parliamentary oversight database and the open web show the figure never entered Italian public discourse. It arrived in August 2026 through an AI deep-research report the author himself had commissioned: the 127-word query stated the thesis as fact; the tool's intermediate plan hedged and promised neutrality; the final output dropped both. All twelve verifiable discrepancies in the draft lean the way the query pointed — a measurable signature of machine-amplified confirmation, audited here with full provenance (query, plan, output attached). The paper then runs the test the interference literature never ran: on 74,629 completed Italian public works, 40.9% of total project time is administrative dead time between phases, where no procedure is open and nothing can be picketed. The interference hypothesis is not refuted. It is redundant. Full provenance and replication package (bilingual editions, original query, research plan, AI-generated draft, code and data) on OSF: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/EKWN2.

title: pyxtabond2: Dynamic Panel GMM Estimation with Interactive Fixed Effects in Python
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: pyxtabond2: Dynamic Panel GMM Estimation with Interactive Fixed Effects in Python
detail.abstract: Dynamic panel data models with a lagged dependent variable require instrumental-variable or generalized method of moments (GMM) treatment to remove the correlation between the regressor and the unobserved individual effect induced by the Nickell (1981) bias. In Stata, Roodman's xtabond2 command (Roodman 2009a) has become the de facto reference implementation of the Arellano and Bond (1991) and Blundell and Bond (1998) estimators, but no equivalent exists in the Python scientific ecosystem, and no existing implementation-in any language-combines a fully GMM-internal-instrument treatment of dynamic panels with estimation under interactive (multifactor) fixed effects. This paper introduces pyxtabond2, a Python package that (i) reproduces xtabond2's matrix algebra and diagnostic tests to a level of fidelity verified line by line against its Mata source and against real Stata output, and (ii) extends it with IFE-GMM, an iterative profile-GMM estimator (Hong et al. 2023) for panels contaminated by interactive fixed effects (Bai 2009), combined with automatic factorcount selection (Bai and Ng 2002; Ahn and Horenstein 2013) and a split-panel jackknife bias correction (Dhaene and Jochmans 2015). We document the statistical framework, the software architecture, and a full validation exercise conducted directly against xtabond2.mata's source and a real Stata run-reported in full alongside every confirmed-correct result and every documented, unresolved limitation-so that any reported number can be traced back to its exact econometric and computational source.

title: MS-SleepNet: A Lightweight Multi-Scale CNN-GRU for Single-Channel EEG Sleep Staging
affiliations: Kyung Hee University, Kyung Hee University and Kyung Hee University

detail.title: MS-SleepNet: A Lightweight Multi-Scale CNN-GRU for Single-Channel EEG Sleep Staging
detail.abstract: Automatic sleep staging from single-channel electroencephalography (EEG) requires both compact representation of intra-epoch patterns and effective modeling of inter-window temporal context. Existing approaches typically target a single accuracy--efficiency operating point, providing little guidance for selecting a model under different resource budgets. We present MS-SleepNet, a lightweight architecture family with three variants (Core, Balance, Edge) built on a shared pipeline that couples a multi-branch depthwise-separable CNN front end with a compact GRU-based temporal encoder; the Edge variant additionally introduces squeeze--excitation recalibration and softmax gated fusion, while all three variants share pointwise-only structured pruning. Across three public datasets (Sleep-EDF-20, Sleep-EDF-78, SHHS) under subject-wise protocols, MS-SleepNet achieves competitive Acc and macro-F1 (MF1) relative to recent single-channel EEG baselines while using fewer parameters, with the Edge variant operating at 9.81K parameters. MS-SleepNet thus offers selectable design points spanning a range of deployment constraints in single-channel EEG sleep staging.

title: TAPM-Net: A Target-Aware Prototype Rectification and Memory Learning Network for Cross-Domain TCM Microscopic Image Classification
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Northeast Forestry University, Northeast Forestry University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: TAPM-Net: A Target-Aware Prototype Rectification and Memory Learning Network for Cross-Domain TCM Microscopic Image Classification
detail.abstract: Different imaging devices introduce substantial domain shifts. These shifts severely degrade the performance of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) microscopic image classification models. Textual descriptions of microscopic identification characteristics provide domain-agnostic semantic anchors for cross-domain classification. However, existing cross-modal classification methods suffer from insufficient discriminability of text prototypes and a bias of visual representations toward seen domains. To address these issues, we propose the Target-Aware Prototype Rectification and Memory Learning Network (TAPM-Net) for cross-domain TCM microscopic image classification. TAPM-Net consists of three stages: text prototype construction, feature adaptation, and decision calibration. In the text prototype construction stage, low-bias text anchors are selected through multi-criteria joint scoring by the Evidence-Driven Cross-Domain Prototype Grounding (ECPG) module. In the feature adaptation stage, source-domain samples are aligned with text prototypes, while target-domain samples are aligned with dynamically updated visual prototypes through dual-signal constraints. A confidence-filtered memory mechanism is further introduced to stabilize prototype estimation. In the decision calibration stage, decision-level correction is performed on low-confidence and high-entropy samples by the Uncertainty-Aware Domain Bias Decoupling (UDBD) module without requiring domain labels. Compared with a non-adaptive baseline, TAPM-Net improves accuracy by up to 11.49 percentage points and weighted F1 by up to 14.31 percentage points on fully unseen target domains. Moreover, TAPM-Net outperforms all competing methods, including test-time adaptation approaches, on unseen domains, while maintaining an accuracy of 0.7622 on the seen target domain.

detail.abstract: This appendix reconstructs the T1–T4 technical family as a bounded architecture of technical and computational functions within the Third Generation in International Relations (3GIR) research programme. The 2026 formulation separates physical and computational infrastructure (T1), system and platform architecture (T2), model and algorithmic logic (T3), and non-human execution functions (T4). The correction removes earlier conflations between technical layers and technical labour, institutional actors, opaque mediation, governance outcomes, data custody, or structural position. A single empirical system may receive several T codes, but each code requires separate evidence and none automatically establishes sovereignty, dependency, W-position, EEE exposure, or algorithmic colonialism. The appendix operationalises the architecture through observable indicators, non-equivalence rules, evidence classes, counter-evidence, falsification conditions, a reusable case-coding protocol, a bounded documentary architecture pilot, and an independent validation design. It also formalises the boundary between T1–T4 and the D1–D3 informational lifecycle, showing why information functions and technical functions may interface frequently without being interchangeable. The central proposition is that technical capacity is analytically meaningful only when the researcher specifies which function is evidenced, who authorises and controls the surrounding arrangement, what neighbouring code families are implicated, and what evidence would weaken the claim.

title: Built for Humans Only? Why AI Adoption in Higher Education Requires a New Deal

detail.title: Built for Humans Only? Why AI Adoption in Higher Education Requires a New Deal
detail.abstract: This paper analyzes the deep structural mismatch between generative AI (GenAI) and the organizational logic of higher education through the lens of institutional economics and organization theory. GenAI defies the traditional worker-or-tool binary assumed by legacy organizational processes, while universities’ vulnerability stems from their reliance on student-made artifacts as proxies for learning and their hesitancy to embrace decisive adaptation efforts that would upset their internal consensus. Endogenous institutional change thus pushes toward marginal patches, especially the addition of layers of new rules while the institutional foundations drift underneath. The paper argues that patching triggers a provenance-verification arms race associated with surveillance creep and pedagogical regression while still failing to restore confidence in legacy assessment practices. Exploring radical alternatives to the standing university model, the paper finds both complete GenAI rejection and its wholesale embrace lacking as mainstream replacements. Its main takeaway from this analysis is that bundling the authentication of student performance with its quantitative evaluation is no longer sustainable within the university. In response, the paper proposes a New Deal Model, which gives up in-house quantitative evaluation (i.e., grades) and focuses instead on documenting the student’s journey. The result is an extensive, machine-readable portfolio, sealed by the university, owned by the student, and unlocked with the student’s consent for downstream gatekeepers, who query it using their own GenAI systems in light of the specific opportunities they offer. Process documentation and a shift toward mentoring-heavy tutelage mitigate concerns about cheating and fabrication. The New Deal Model preserves the community aspect of higher education and the marriage of teaching, research, and public epistemic authority while increasing institutional GenAI compatibility and future-proofness – as GenAI advances, thin, grade-based datasets depreciate while thick, data-rich portfolios appreciate. The paper charts a gradual transition path in which portfolios temporarily run in parallel with legacy grading. Such a transition allows a side-by-side test of the paper’s central bet, namely, that GenAI evaluation of authenticated process records will predict real-world performance better than current grade-based assessment does.

title: Migration and Social Remittances: Different Lenses from Social Sciences
affiliations: and Alpen-Adria-University Klagenfurt

detail.title: Migration and Social Remittances: Different Lenses from Social Sciences
detail.abstract: Migration is often viewed through an economic lens, but it also drives a profound transfer of intangible resources, including ideas, attitudes, beliefs, practices, values, and norms. This review examines the emerging literature on social remittances across post-transition economies. These countries are characterized by their shift from socialist planning to market-oriented systems. Based on an analysis of twenty-six publications, this literature review examines the mechanisms through which intangible resources are acquired, transferred, and implemented among migrants, their communities of origin, and even their destination societies. The evidence reveals that migrants often act as agents of change, transferring knowledge and practices that influence areas from entrepreneurship and politics to science, gender norms, and everyday life. Future research should analyze the social networks, structural constraints, and digital tools that facilitate these knowledge transfers across the skill spectrum. Such work is important for developing holistic policies that can leverage the social remittances of diverse migrant groups as a sustained resource for social innovation and development in evolving economies.

title: Experimentation under Delayed Success
affiliations: Shiv Nadar University and Shiv Nadar University

detail.title: Experimentation under Delayed Success
detail.abstract: We study a dynamic principal-agent model of experimentation in an environment with delayed success and inconclusive failures. An agent allocates effort between a safe option and a risky alternative that yields higher long-run payoffs but a lower success rate. In this setting, standard success-based incentives are ineffective, as they induce the agent to shift effort toward safer activities that generate more frequent successes. We show that efficient experimentation can be implemented with a simple linear contract that rewards failures and penalizes successes. We fully characterize the set of contracts that sustain efficient behavior and show that the optimal contract is typically reward-dominant and may rely entirely on rewarding failures. Methodologically, we introduce a mixed-news bandit framework in which successes are conclusive while failures are not, and show that smooth pasting holds despite the presence of bad news.

detail.abstract: The state of world economy and foreign trade International organizations, including the World Bank, IMF, OECD, WTO, and UN, point out that the global economy will be stable in 2025, even with a bunch of challenges. According to their estimates, global GDP growth in 2025 ranged from 2.7% (according to the World Bank) to 3.3% (according to the IMF) and will remain at this level in 2026 and 2027. According to the latest data from the International Monetary Fund, 2 published in January 2026, global economic growth in 2025 remained at the previous year's level of 3.3%. Forecasts indicate that global economic growth will remain stable at 3.3% in 2026 and slow slightly to 3.2% in 2027 (Table 1). This stability is due to the balanced impact of various factors. Negative trends associated with changes in trade policy are offset by positive aspects such as increased investment in technology, especially artificial intelligence (AI), which is most noticeable in North America and Asia. Fiscal and monetary support, favorable financial conditions, and private sector.

title: TWFF: An Open Event Log Format for Studying Writing Processes in AI-Assisted Environments
affiliations: and Functional Intelligence Research Lab

detail.title: TWFF: An Open Event Log Format for Studying Writing Processes in AI-Assisted Environments
detail.abstract: AI text detectors are now the dominant institutional response to generative AI in education. This paper argues that this response is architecturally flawed: classifiers trained to estimate whether text was machine-generated cannot produce the auditable, non-discriminatory evidence that educational and regulatory contexts require. We document three core failure modes: high false positive rates affecting non-native English writers, adversarial evasion, and non-compliance with EU AI Act transparency requirements, and then we propose a different approach. The Tracked Writing File Format (TWFF) is an open source ZIP-based container standard that records the writing process as a deterministic event log. Rather than inferring AI involvement from final text, TWFF captures what occurred during composition: edit sessions, paste events, AI interactions, and revision sequences. The author retains ownership of this record and discloses it voluntarily. We describe the format specification, the design principles behind its architecture, a reference implementation (Colophon, a browser extension for Google Docs), and the use cases that the format enables. The specification and reference implementation are available at https://github.com/Functional-Intelligence-Research-Lab/twff

The author has a financial interest in the commercial application of the methodology this paper tests.

detail.abstract: Portfolio construction follows conventions that determine what a fund holds, how long it holds it, and how many positions it runs. This paper tests three of those conventions against 126,144 published equity portfolios. Every portfolio in the permutation grid is reported, so the paper is a census rather than a sample, and no configuration was selected on its result. Every entry price published the Sunday before its trading window opened. Every portfolio enters on a Temporal Structural Forecasting signal, and one construction decision varies at a time. Across 17,280 portfolios, universes defined by how a stock trades outperformed universes defined by what the business does, on median return, on the share of portfolios profitable, and on the share positive in every closed year. Across 34,992 matched pairs, the 240 rule beat a forced exit at day 120 in 90.2% of pairs, at a median drawdown difference of 0.00 percentage points. Across 51,840 portfolios, raising position size from 10 to 100 took the best five-year return from 34.39% to 13.38% and the count of portfolios beating the index from 341 to none. The best portfolio in the population returned 34.39% annualized with no losing year. The 876 portfolios that exceeded the S&P 500 did so at a median capital exposure of 69.2%.

title: How Must Law Evolve When Technology, Climate Change and Global Economic Power Outpace the Traditional Institutions of the State

detail.title: How Must Law Evolve When Technology, Climate Change and Global Economic Power Outpace the Traditional Institutions of the State
detail.abstract: The nation-state's legislative and adjudicative cycles were built for a world in which technological change, ecological disruption, and the concentration of economic power moved on generational or, at most, decadal timescales. That assumption no longer holds. Frontier artificial intelligence systems are deployed and revised faster than administrative rulemaking can respond; climate feedback loops are compressing decision windows that international law still treats as open-ended; and a small number of transnational corporate actors now command balance sheets and infrastructural control exceeding those of most sovereign states, without corresponding public-law accountability. This article asks how legal systems can restore institutional synchrony with the phenomena they are meant to govern, and argues that the central deficiency is not an absence of substantive norms but a structural mismatch between the temporality of law-making and the temporality of the governed phenomena-a condition this article terms institutional desynchronization. Employing a doctrinal, comparative, and institutional-empirical methodology across the European Union, the United States, China, Brazil, and India, and situating the analysis against the jurisprudence of Urgenda v. Netherlands, Massachusetts v. EPA, Neubauer v. Germany, and Held v. Montana, the article develops the Institutional Adaptive Capacity Standard (IACS), a governance architecture built on continuous-review rulemaking, sunset-triggered delegated authority, and pre-committed judicial deference calibrated to demonstrated regulatory responsiveness rather than to agency status alone. The article contributes an original diagnostic framework for measuring a legal system's temporal capacity and a concrete, testable institutional design for closing the desynchronization gap without abandoning rule-of-law constraints on delegated power.

title: DistillSem: LLM-Distilled Financial Headline Semantics for Cross-Sectional Return Prediction

detail.title: DistillSem: LLM-Distilled Financial Headline Semantics for Cross-Sectional Return Prediction
detail.abstract: Many stock prediction systems using financial news headlines compress each headline into a single sentiment polarity score. This compression discards information about what happened, how strongly it should matter, and over what horizon its price impact is likely to unfold. This paper studies whether structured event semantics distilled from large language models (LLMs) provide predictive information beyond polarity-based sentiment baselines. We propose DISTILLSEM, which distills these semantics into a lightweight headline representation. An LLM teacher annotates headlines along six market-relevant dimensions (event type, directional sentiment, signal strength, market relevance, price-impact horizon, and labeling confidence), while term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF) logistic regression classifiers learn the four discrete dimensions, yielding a structured semantic representation that can be computed efficiently at corpus scale. Using 96,802 teacher labels spanning 2015 to 2022, our best distilled representation yields an information coefficient (IC) of 0.0225 (t = 3.80) on a heldout cross-sectional return ranking task covering 2024 to 2026. Under the same evaluation protocol, FinBERT polarity features (IC = 0.0004) and a direct lexical baseline that uses a matching TF-IDF text representation but receives no LLM supervision (IC = 0.0056) have conventional t statistics below the reference threshold. Controlled ablations further reveal a temporal alignment effect. Teacher labels collected from the period closest to the downstream evaluation regime yield substantially stronger predictive signals than larger label sets collected from earlier market regimes. Permutation tests that hold daily news coverage fixed (p ≤ 0.006) show that the signal cannot be explained by coverage artifacts alone.

title: Normalization as an Attention Budget A Representation Theorem and a Test

detail.title: Normalization as an Attention Budget A Representation Theorem and a Test
detail.abstract: Models of social preference routinely normalize the weights an individual places on others so that they sum to a constant: the divisor 1/(n-1) in Fehr and Schmidt (1999), the unit row sum in Snidal (1991), implicitly the comparison to the mean in Bolton and Ockenfels (2000). Fehr and Schmidt state the convention's purpose in invariance terms - it makes the relative impact of the fairness term independent of the number of players - and the description stops at the utility function. This paper argues that the convention asserts more: it is a substantive hypothesis about interpersonal attention - that regard for others is a fixed budget divided among them - and the paper gives the hypothesis a foundation, two consequences, and a test. The foundation: three axioms on a preference relation over payoff profiles - order with continuity, translation invariance, and own-monotonicity - are equivalent to the representation U_i(x) = x_i - sum_j w_ij x_j, with the weight vector exactly unique rather than unique up to transformation; the budget k = sum_j w_ij is then a defined quantity recoverable from a single indifference, and the normalization is isolated as one further axiom, population invariance of k, testable by repeating that elicitation at different group sizes. First consequence: in the linear voluntary-contribution mechanism the marginal incentive to contribute is exactly (m-1) - alpha*phi + beta*psi, where phi and psi are the fractions of the group contributing less and more than the subject; group size enters at no contribution profile, generalizing the corner statement of Barcelo and Capraro (2015). The large-group experimental record is consistent with the null; where a group-size effect appears, we argue it indicts the budget rather than the preferences - a distinction contribution data cannot make and the elicitation can. Second consequence: transposed to a bargaining problem, Snidal's normalization makes the number of actors inert for the existence of a mutually acceptable division, the opposite of the conclusion he draws from it; the proof is self-contained here. We close with the unconstrained matrix, in whose columns - regard received rather than distributed - the behaviourally relevant structure lies, and with the experimental design that the axioms constitute.

title: Proof of Honesty, Not Proof of Fraud Asymmetric Trust Infrastructure for Smallholder Provenance

detail.title: Proof of Honesty, Not Proof of Fraud Asymmetric Trust Infrastructure for Smallholder Provenance
detail.abstract: Provenance technology is overwhelmingly built to answer the question "is this product fake?". We argue that this framing systematically disadvantages the producers it is nominally meant to protect. Anti-counterfeiting is an arms race in which the defender must be right every time, and, more importantly, it places the cost of proof on whoever must comply-which is why audit-based certification prices out smallholders, and why due-diligence regimes such as the EU Deforestation Regulation now put their market access at risk. We invert the objective. Rather than making forgery impossible, we make honesty cheap to demonstrate and differentially expensive to imitate. We present the design of Trace, an implemented and publicly available provenance system for smallholder farmers and artisan makers, and articulate its central architectural idea: asymmetric trust infrastructure. Key management is a burden proportional to institutional capacity, so Trace places it only where that capacity exists. Origin records are keyless and content-addressed, created offline on a commodity phone by a producer who has no keys to lose. Intermediate custody-carriers, warehouses, exporters-is cryptographically signed, because logistics firms can run a root key and delegate to staff devices. The final receipt at the last mile is keyless again, because a consumer will not enrol. Both human ends of the chain stay frictionless; signatures appear only in the institutional middle. We give a per-layer threat model that states precisely what each mechanism does and does not guarantee, and we are explicit that origin authenticity is not a cryptographic property of this system but a social one, resting on witnesses and accumulated multi-party history. We argue this is the correct place for it to rest. We conclude with a detailed evaluation protocol; the studies it specifies have not yet been run, and we present this as a design paper rather than an empirical one.

title: Big Data Machine Learning Portfolios in Thirty Minute SPX Options
affiliations: , Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Karlsruhe Institute of Technology and Karlsruhe Institute of Technology

detail.title: Big Data Machine Learning Portfolios in Thirty Minute SPX Options
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether 30-minute delta-hedged returns on S&P 500 index options are predictable using machine learning. Using 14 million high-frequency observations from 2015 and a set of 69 predictors, we examine how feature selection and model complexity affect forecasting performance. We find economically and statistically significant predictability. Disciplined feature selection can improve outof-sample accuracy and profitability. Forecast combinations achieve out-of-sample R2 values of 2.7-3.1% and generate decile portfolios with 30-minute gross Sharpe ratios above 0.60, indicating economically meaningful intraday predictability. We find option mispricing to be the main driver behind our results.

title: Religion as Informal Governance: Evidence from the SOX-Era Reforms
affiliations: Western Michigan University

detail.title: Religion as Informal Governance: Evidence from the SOX-Era Reforms
detail.abstract: The corporate governance literature has traditionally emphasized formal governance mechanisms that constrain managerial opportunism. However, firms are embedded in local social environments whose norms may influence managerial behavior. I examine whether local religious culture serves as an informal governance mechanism and whether its influence depends on the strength of formal governance. I find that firms in more religious counties exhibit significantly lower idiosyncratic risk. A one-standard-deviation increase in county religiosity is associated with a 0.96 percentage point reduction in annualized volatility. Using the Sarbanes-Oxley Act and related exchange reforms as a broad strengthening of formal governance, I show that this relation attenuates substantially and becomes statistically indistinguishable from zero. The results are consistent with substitution between formal and informal governance mechanisms. The adoption of majority-independent boards reduces risk primarily in firms located in less religious areas, and firms that relocate to more religious counties experience reductions in risk. Further, lower pre-reform risk is not accompanied by lower firm value, indicating that risk aversion of religious cultures does not fully explain the baseline results.

title: Central Bank Digital Currencies and the Transformation of the Monetary Policy Transmission Mechanism
affiliations: Moscow State University of International Relations (MGIMO University)

detail.title: Central Bank Digital Currencies and the Transformation of the Monetary Policy Transmission Mechanism
detail.abstract: The digitalization of the financial sector is giving rise to new forms of money, foremost among them central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) and private digital payment instruments. These changes affect not only the form of money itself but also the mechanism through which monetary policy is transmitted to the real economy. Under the traditional model, transmission relies on the banking channel: the central bank shapes liquidity conditions, and commercial banks pass this impulse on to the real sector through lending. Digitalization, however, is creating alternative channels through which the central bank can potentially interact with economic agents directly. This paper examines the degree to which digital forms of money are transforming the monetary policy transmission mechanism and altering the role of the banking sector. Drawing on Bank for International Settlements (BIS) survey data, European Central Bank (ECB) modelling evidence, and a comparative institutional analysis of the United States, the European Union, and Russia, the paper argues that digitalization does not lead to a unified outcome but instead produces several competing national configurations of monetary transmission.

detail.abstract: Israel faces a growing financial governance challenge in Gaza. As the territory's formal economy collapses and informal financial networks expand, Israeli authorities have less visibility into financial activity while Israeli banks face increasing compliance and counterterror financing risks. This brief argues that a tightly controlled, US-regulated, dollar-backed stablecoin system offers a practical alternative to the current approach. By creating a transparent digital payment infrastructure under joint US-Israeli oversight, Israel could improve financial transparency, strengthen counterterror financing enforcement, reduce risks to its banking sector, and preserve greater strategic flexibility while managing Gaza's long-term economic instability.

title: Neural Attention in Heterogeneous-Agent Economies
affiliations: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago

detail.title: Neural Attention in Heterogeneous-Agent Economies

publicationDetails.detailsText: FRB of Chicago Working Paper No. 2026-14
publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Transformers, the neural-network architecture behind much of modern AI, combine flexible nonlinear approximation with an attention mechanism that learns how information is combined across inputs. Can neural attention reveal which parts of an agent distribution matter for aggregate dynamics? I represent economic states as tokens—such as wealth bins, capital, debt, and productivity—and embed a transformer in a recursive Krusell–Smith-style solution method. The transformer forecasts the continuation tokenized distribution entering individual Bellman equations. Its neural-network component approximates nonlinear aggregate policy functions, while attention learns how distributional information is aggregated and yields interpretable weights. In Krusell–Smith benchmarks, the transformer rediscovers approximate aggregation, assigning nearly uniform attention across the distribution when aggregate capital is nearly sufficient. In a heterogeneous-firm economy with endogenous default, attention instead concentrates near the default margin and rises during crises for financially constrained firms when their default risk becomes more consequential for aggregate dynamics. Attention therefore serves simultaneously as a solution device and a diagnostic of economic aggregation.

title: Massive Markets, Localized Prices: The Microeconomics of Gas in Farmington

detail.title: Massive Markets, Localized Prices: The Microeconomics of Gas in Farmington
detail.abstract: This paper examines different gasoline 86 prices across different gas stations in Farmington, New Mexico. The main research question was: Why is gasoline priced differently within the same city? Information from six different gas stations across Farmington, including the prices of gasoline 86, diesel, Lay's salt and vinegar chips, and Aquafina water. Overall, I found that there are many different factors that lead to the price differences in these nearby gas stations, including location, convenience, competition, strategy, branding, loyalty programs, and false deals.

title: Spiritual Intelligence in Public Administration: Toward a Theory of Meaning-Centered and Transformative Governance
affiliations: African Research Network (ARN)

detail.title: Spiritual Intelligence in Public Administration: Toward a Theory of Meaning-Centered and Transformative Governance
detail.abstract: Contemporary public administration has developed sophisticated capacities for organizational coordination, performance management, evidence-based decision-making, and technological innovation. Yet many of the problems confronting contemporary governance-including institutional distrust, ecological disruption, technological transformation, social fragmentation, and persistent collective-action failures-cannot be resolved through instrumental capacity alone. The central problem is not simply whether public institutions can act effectively, but whether they can determine what is worth pursuing, reconcile competing values, sustain collective purpose, and adapt responsibly under conditions of uncertainty. This article develops a theory of Spiritual Intelligence in Public Administration (SIPA), conceptualizing spiritual intelligence not as religious belief, private spirituality, or a form of psychological well-being, but as a higher-order capacity for meaning-making, ethical discernment, relational awareness, long-term orientation, and purpose-directed action. Building on scholarship on public value, collaborative governance, adaptive leadership, public-service ethics, spirituality in public administration, and complex governance, the article argues that spiritual intelligence can be understood as a potential governance capacity rather than merely an individual attribute. The article proposes a theoretical sequence in which spiritual intelligence contributes to institutional wisdom, defined as the capacity of governance systems to integrate knowledge, values, experience, relationships, uncertainty, and long-term consequences when making collective decisions. Institutional wisdom, in turn, provides a potential foundation for meaning-centered and transformative governance. The article makes three theoretical contributions. First, it extends public-administration debates beyond the conventional opposition between bureaucratic rationality and collaborative governance by introducing meaning, purpose, and transcendence as dimensions of administrative capability. Second, it distinguishes spiritual intelligence from spirituality and spiritual leadership and relocates the construct from the individual level toward organizational and governance-system levels. Third, it proposes the Spiritual Intelligence-Institutional Wisdom-Transformative Governance (SI-IW-TG) framework as a basis for future empirical research. The argument is not that spirituality should replace administrative rationality, nor that public institutions should adopt religious doctrine. Rather, it is that complex governance requires an additional capacity to reflect upon the purposes, values, relationships, and long-term consequences that technical rationality alone cannot determine.

title: More Strategies, Same Zero: Multiple Testing Against LLM-Scale Alpha Search
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: More Strategies, Same Zero: Multiple Testing Against LLM-Scale Alpha Search

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no personal or financial relationships with other people or organizations that could have influenced this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. The study uses only publicly available market data (FRED and Yahoo Finance daily series) and involves no human subjects or personal data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Large language models can propose and backtest trading strategies at effectively unbounded scale, reviving an old hazard — backtest overfitting — in a new regime where the number of trials N is enormous and cheap. We ask whether scaling LLM-style strategy search accumulates genuine edge or only statistically false discoveries that vanish under proper multiple-testing correction. Using a pure-Python alpha engine with a deliberately brutal verifier (causal next-bar execution, transaction costs, worst-of-regimes out-of-sample scoring, and a deflated-Sharpe multiple-testing haircut; Bailey & López de Prado 2014), we sweep N from 10 to 3,000 across three generators — uniform-random, Boden-operator "creative" synthesis, and a live LLM proposer (Claude Opus 4.8) — on four markets: a strong planted edge (positive control), a realistically small planted edge (power control), a pure random-walk null, and real S&P 500 data (FRED, 2016–2024). We find: (1) the naive single-holdout best-of-N Sharpe rises monotonically with N on every market, including pure noise (+0.04→+0.34) and real S&P 500 (+0.72→+0.99 annualized), reproducing the false-strategy theorem with a generative search engine, the live LLM included; (2) the deflated worst-regime gate holds survivors at exactly 0 on the real market for all N and all three generators, while recovering the strong planted edge (survivors grow with N) — it discriminates, it is not a blanket reject; (3) a gate power surface — our central characterization (and the empirical instantiation, across generator types and with calibrated controls, of Bailey–López de Prado's expected-max-of-N result, not a new theorem): the gate admits an edge only once its true worst-regime Sharpe clears the multiple-testing floor (~2.3 at N=1,000), so a moderate real edge (Sharpe ~1–2) is also rejected — scaling the search raises the discovery bar (≈√(2 ln N)) faster than search finds edge, making moderate edges unprovable at scale; (4) an ablation shows worst-regime robustness alone is insufficient on real data (it admits 115–196 "robust" mirages that grow with N) and the deflation is load-bearing; (5) the standard deflation is in fact over-conservative for the worst-of-regimes statistic (the single-Sharpe DSR over-deflates it ~2.4× for our 3-regime gate — a k-dependent factor, 1.65×/2.35×/4.32× at k=2/3/5, not a universal constant, §4.9), yet the real-market zero survives the corrected, much weaker bar — so the conclusion is not an over-deflation artifact, and the assumption-free bootstrap independently agrees; (6) creative and LLM search manufacture more original-looking mirages than random but convert zero to survivors, amplifying a real edge ~5× only when one exists. We conclude that LLM-scale search manufactures false discoveries, and that the only correction that stops them simultaneously renders moderate genuine edges unprovable at this search scale. The result generalizes: it holds under a distribution-free block-bootstrap test (White/Romano–Wolf/Hansen), on a real cross-sectional equity panel (range/volume features active), and across three microstructurally-independent real markets (FX, gold, crypto) — seven real markets, zero survivors at every N — and the live LLM, extended to N=300, reproduces it. We also derive the worst-of-regimes deflation the gate actually needs — the standard single-Sharpe DSR over-deflates the min-over-regimes statistic by ~2.4× — and show the real-market zero is robust even to that much weaker, correct bar; this yields a unifying "robustness dividend" (requiring worst-of-k independent regimes ≈ deflating a thousand-strategy search to N′≈7), which collapses precisely when regimes correlate — on the pinned data snapshot real S&P 500 measures ρ_reg≈0.37 → N′≈24, and an earlier mid-2026 snapshot of the same series measured ρ_reg≈0.67 → N′≈84; the collapse is real but its magnitude is snapshot-sensitive (~3–12×), an instability that itself argues the dividend cannot be budgeted on and explicit deflation must carry the load on real data. We report two cautionary negatives in the same spirit: two analytic effective-trials shortcuts (a genomics participation-ratio import; an envelope-inversion) both fail, leaving the block bootstrap as the necessary arbiter. The contribution is the controlled multi-generator demonstration (live LLM included), the power-surface precision/recall characterization, the derived worst-of-regimes deflation and robustness-dividend identity, and the distribution-free confirmation — all reproducible, with a verification suite at 20/20 and 38 math/invariant unit tests.

title: Sri Lanka Investment Climate Report 2026 (European Union)

detail.title: Sri Lanka Investment Climate Report 2026 (European Union)
detail.abstract: This report assesses Sri Lanka's investment climate in 2026, a moment poised between post-crisis stabilization and the pursuit of sustained, investment-led growth. Following the 2022 economic crisis, consistent reform and improved macroeconomic management restored stability, with reserves rebuilding to roughly three months of import cover, moderating inflation, and 5% growth in 2025. That recovery is now being tested by two shocks, Cyclone Ditwah and the Middle East crisis triggered by the Iran war, which have raised energy and freight costs and prompted the IMF to revise growth down to 3% for 2026. Drawing on World Bank Enterprise Survey data, stakeholder consultations, and benchmarking against India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Malaysia, Vietnam, and Singapore, the report finds that Sri Lanka underperforms its regional peers on nearly every dimension of the business environment, from licensing, tax administration, and VAT refunds to utility connections, judicial independence, and trade facilitation. The binding constraints are shown to be fragmented and uncoordinated agencies, manual and discretionary procedures, and policy unpredictability rather than any single legal deficiency. The report also examines the centrality of the European Union as an export market and source of high-quality FDI, the strategic implications of the newly concluded EU–India trade agreement for GSP+ and the proposed ETCA, and four sectors of comparative advantage, renewable energy, ports and shipping, IT-BPM, and tourism. It concludes that converting stabilization into durable growth will depend on macroeconomic discipline, stronger inter-agency coordination, deeper trade liberalization, and predictable policy, with continued EU partnership remaining vital.

detail.title: The Adaptive Sovereign Balance Framework at Its Boundary: A Test on the Issuer of the World's Reserve Currency

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses only publicly available macroeconomic and institutional data; no human subjects or participant data were involved.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this research.

detail.abstract: This paper tests the Adaptive Sovereign Balance Framework (ASBF) against a case its own scope conditions anticipate but do not resolve: the issuer of the world’s principal reserve currency. Where prior applications establish the architecture’s reproducibility within one narrow class — small open, commodity-dependent economies with a comparable sovereign wealth fund — the present paper deliberately tests its boundary. One contour (D2, inter-temporal transfer) is shown not to exist at the US federal level; four candidate institutions are examined and rejected on distinct grounds. Two others (D3, D4) are shown to have drifted, in earlier work, from their defined functions; correcting D3 surfaces a positive finding — a debt-maturity-structure measure that produced a real-time signal in 2008–09 where two alternatives were silent — and a negative one, that the distributionally correct measure (Revenues over Mandatory Spending plus Net Interest) rises rather than falls during the exact 2011–2019 period of debt accumulation it was sought to detect, through the same rate-endogeneity mechanism documented elsewhere in the paper. The paper’s central, load-bearing finding concerns the framework’s dynamic-pressure axis: for a price-maker at the centre of the global financial system, a shock’s causal origin and the sovereign’s own policy response are not separable as the small-open-economy architecture presupposes, so that R_i’s standard reading as “incoming pressure” is constructively violated — demonstrated across four episodes (1975, 1982, 2020, and the 1998 Russian default, chosen because its trigger was unambiguously external) and confirmed not to extend, by the same mechanism, to the monetary-credibility contour, instead shown to carry a bias toward false alarm rather than false calm. Separately, reserve-currency status is shown far stickier than any of four tested fundamentals — economic weight, export complexity, hard-power capacity, sovereign debt-market depth — consistent with a coordination-equilibrium reading, with sterling’s inverse trajectory as the decisive case; this motivates formalising the paper’s regime-exhaustion construct as a survival-analysis object, while showing why the available sample cannot support its formal estimation. A further, general architectural gap — sovereign capacity to backstop a distressed financial system — is identified independently through two routes and confirmed for both the United States and Kazakhstan. Beyond the single-year illustration, working candidates are constructed and tested — not merely proposed — for the two weight parameters (L1, L4) the framework’s original construction left blocked. For D1, the ratio of Treasury debt held by the public to total non-financial private credit, motivated by a safe-asset-scarcity mechanism and evaluated against a dated registry of publicly legible events rather than NBER recession dates, shows pressure-axis deviations significantly concentrated around such events (p=0.011, n=62 years); combined with M3 and the current-account balance into a three-contour pressure index, the result holds over the same window. For D4, a residual isolating the portion of professional forecasters’ long-run inflation expectations not explained by the current policy rate — constructed to track fiscal dominance (Sargent and Wallace, 1981) — is independently significant (p=0.018) and, folded into a four-contour index using placeholder equal weights, remains significant over a shorter window (p=0.013, n=43). Realised inflation, tested separately as a check, outperforms it on the same test, read against the paper’s own finding that US CPI’s shelter component cannot register asset-price booms. A single-year illustration is also presented, explicitly as such: the full five-contour weighting architecture, and thresholds for two contours, remain open, including a specific institutional discontinuity — the elimination of reserve requirements in 2020 — that renders one Kazakhstan-derived construction inapplicable to recent US data by definition. The paper’s contribution is a map of where and why the architecture requires adaptation for this class of economy, together with tested — not only illustrative — evidence for two of its most contested parameters, not a fully validated vulnerability index for the United States.

title: Solving a Large Multi-Sector New Keynesian Quarterly Projection Model in Python
affiliations: Innovation and Digital Development Agency

detail.title: Solving a Large Multi-Sector New Keynesian Quarterly Projection Model in Python
detail.abstract: This paper solves a large multi-sector New Keynesian quarterly projection model entirely in opensource Python. Quarterly projection models are becoming essential tools in modern policy analysis, yet they remain small in structure and are solved using proprietary software. This paper relaxes both constraints at once. The model combines the canonical forecasting-and-policyanalysis core with four extensions tailored to a small open oil-exporting economy. The paper integrates a ten-sector non-oil supply alongside an oil sector, an endogenous oil-geared fiscal block that serves as the principal distributor of oil wealth to domestic actors, a banking and credit block with imperfect retail-rate pass-through, loan quality, and liquidity, and geopolitical risk as an explicit exogenous driver. The resulting system of forty-three behavioural equations is solved by the extended-path method, which handles the model's nonlinearities, the sectoral aggregation, and the piecewise policy rule exactly rather than by linearization. As a result, in recursive out-ofsample forecasts, the model outperforms an ARIMA benchmark for 37 of 43 variables, reducing average RMSE from 9.2 to 5.5. To the author's knowledge, this is the first large multi-sector projection model of its kind implemented in a fully open Python environment, which eliminates the barriers to accessing expensive software platforms and specialized solution tools required to use large-scale models. In doing so, it removes the obstacles that have traditionally limited the use of a large sector-wide model in decision-making by central banks, ministries of finance and economy, and major commercial banks.

reference: Strategic Management Journal, volume 47, issue 7, 2026[10.1002/smj.70079]
title: When does Category Spanning Hurt or Help Producers?
affiliations: State University of New York, Stony Brook,  and University of Notre Dame

detail.title: When does Category Spanning Hurt or Help Producers?

publicationDetails.detailsText: Strategic Management Journal, volume 47, issue 7, 2026[10.1002/smj.70079]

detail.abstract:
Scholars have theorized many factors shaping whether category spanning helps or hurts producers. We first synthesize evidence by meta-analyzing 25 years of empirical research, which reveals a null effect of spanning on average, yet with significant subsample heterogeneity. To unpack it, we theorize and find that spanning hurts producers more (i) when spanning occurs within bounded (vs. unbounded) category systems, (ii) when category associations are made by third parties (vs. insiders), (iii) when spanning is located at the product (vs. producer) level, and (iv) when spanning is occurring at once (vs. over time). Two mechanisms underpin these relationships: on the audience side, spanning influences evaluations when it is salient; on the producer side, spanning results in more positive outcomes when producers can control how their spanning behavior is conveyed to audiences. Because these two mechanisms operate jointly, their combined influence can result in spanning having a null, a positive, or a negative net effect. Our study identifies, across 16 theoretical configurations, where these three baseline effects should be expected and clarifies why.

Managerial Summary

Firms face a strategic dilemma: should they span across categories or stay focused? Prior studies show mixed results on whether spanning helps or hurts performance. Our findings suggest that outcomes depend on how salient spanning is to audiences and how controllable it is for producers. Spanning tends to hurt performance (i) when the categorization system is bounded (vs. unbounded), (ii) when third parties (vs. insiders) highlight the diversification, (iii) when individual products (vs. producers) span categories, and (iv) when spanning occurs simultaneously (vs. over time). Firms can benefit from spanning, but success depends on managing these four factors to reduce saliency and enhance controllability.

title: Organizational Risk Perception in Public Agencies: The Role of Contracting and Scientific and Professional Information
affiliations: and Arizona State University (ASU) - Center for Science, Technology and Environmental Policy Studies

detail.title: Organizational Risk Perception in Public Agencies: The Role of Contracting and Scientific and Professional Information

declarations.ethicsApproval: The Human Research Ethics Committee at Arizona State University approved this study (study #00003589). All survey respondents provided informed consent prior to participation.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by funding from Center for Science, Technology and Environmental Policy Studies (C-STEPS) at ASU

detail.abstract: Public agencies are increasingly required to respond to multiple and evolving threats. Perceptions of risk are important triggers of organizational responses and motivate adaptive strategies. Integrating administrative data with a survey of public managers employed across the 300 largest transit agencies in the US, we examine how outsourcing decisions and reliance on scientific and professional sources of information influence public agencies’ perceptions of extreme weather events’ risks. Results show that reliance on scientific and professional sources of information is positively associated with perceived risk of extreme weather events. The effect of contracting on risk perceptions depends on agencies’ outsourcing strategies.

title: Already Illegal: Flock Safety and the Six Bodies of Existing Law Nobody Is Applying

detail.title: Already Illegal: Flock Safety and the Six Bodies of Existing Law Nobody Is Applying
detail.abstract: Automated license plate reader networks are debated as a privacy problem awaiting a privacy statute. That debate has obscured a simpler fact: at least six bodies of existing law already reach the conduct, and none of them is a privacy statute. Antidiscrimination law reaches the procurement decision, because a municipality that closes its own mobility program to a disability-defined class through a facially neutral administrative choice violates Title II and Section 504. State criminal surveillance law reaches the conduct, because observing a person in a private place without the consent of all persons observed is a felony in Georgia and in most states. Consumer protection law reaches the vendor, on a deception theory and on an unfairness theory grounded in documented security failure. Contract and delegated authority reach the access, because a municipality cannot license to a vendor a use that the camera owner was expressly told would not occur. Computer crime law reaches the intruder but, after Van Buren v. United States, not the credentialed insider, and that hole is the one real gap. National security data law reaches the location data itself, because the executive branch has already found by regulation that precise geolocation inside 736 enumerated areas is government-related data regardless of volume. This Article also reports an original empirical result bearing on the last of those. Joining the coordinates the Attorney General published for all 736 areas against 23,946 mapped readers, the author finds readers inside 74 enumerated areas, 504 of them within tightly drawn boundaries, against 11,992 within a ten kilometer approach. The densest is a 2.14 square kilometer rectangle enclosing the Pentagon, which holds eleven readers positioned on the roads in and out. The Article assembles the six bodies, identifies the statute the public reaches for and why it fails, and closes on the substitution the enacted threat model has not performed: what the assembled system does when the tracked vehicle belongs to a sitting legislator and the credentials belong to someone who can be bought.

title: Arbitration of FRAND Disputes

detail.title: Arbitration of FRAND Disputes
detail.abstract: Recent litigation concerning SEPs has thrown into stark relief the contrast between the territoriality of patents on the one hand and the global nature of standards, and hence the FRAND obligation, on the other hand. This has led to jurisdictional battles, races to the court, anti-suit injunctions and even anti-anti-suit injunctions. The most satisfactory answer to these problems is to have a global system of arbitration of FRAND disputes. In order for such a system to work properly, it needs to be legally enforceable. This chapter sets out how this can be done, and answers objections that have been raised to the proposal.

title: Consumption Ratcheting and Borrowing Constraints
affiliations: Kyung Hee University - Department of Applied Mathematics

detail.title: Consumption Ratcheting and Borrowing Constraints
detail.abstract: We solve an infinite-horizon consumption-portfolio problem with irreversible consumption, deterministic income, and nonnegative financial wealth. Ratcheting itself imposes a solvency floor, so the effective state constraint is kinked: the hard borrowing boundary is active below labor income, whereas ratcheting solvency dominates above it. The latter region is the classical homothetic problem; the former contains a finite dual borrowing boundary jointly determined with the consumption boundary. We reduce the two boundaries to a singular scalar ODE. Its economically relevant solution is selected by asymptotic matching rather than by an endpoint value, and the dual borrowing boundary satisfies an explicit power-law escape while the consumption boundary converges to the classical threshold. We construct the global dual solution and verify optimality through an obliquely reflected dual diffusion. In the reconstructed primal wealth equation, the borrowing and consumption regulators vanish through two distinct contact identities.

title: Remittance and Climate Resilient Agricultural Technology Adoption: Evidence from Shyamnagar Upazila, Bangladesh

detail.title: Remittance and Climate Resilient Agricultural Technology Adoption: Evidence from Shyamnagar Upazila, Bangladesh
