detail.abstract: The daily reset of leveraged and inverse exchange-traded funds implies a predictable end-ofday exposure adjustment, but it says nothing about the instrument used to carry that adjustment out. We examine Korea's simultaneous launch of single-name leveraged and inverse ETFs, matching official portfolio-composition files to intraday prices for the ETFs, their underlying stocks, and the corresponding single-stock futures. Published creation baskets route a large share of directional notional through futures, and the share differs even across funds with the same underlying stock and the same leverage target. Our central test compares products within stock-date cells: when futures move after the ETF and cash markets have already closed, funds with greater leverage-weighted disclosed futures exposure show a more negative gap between the ETF close and official NAV. The relation holds up across alternative specifications, subsamples, and contract-roll exclusions. At the market level, accounting-implied reset pressure lines up more strongly with futures returns than with cash-stock returns over part of the afternoon, though this depends on the chosen window and execution-level hedge records are unavailable. Quote-based post-close futures-cash adjustment looks similar in treated and untreated stocks. Disclosed futures composition thus predicts cross-product differences in closing gaps created by asynchronous market closes, while the basis adjustment itself is not specific to treated stocks.

title: Pricing (Some) Cryptocurrencies
affiliations: HKU Business School, The University of Hong Kong and The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Business and Economics

detail.title: Pricing (Some) Cryptocurrencies
detail.abstract: The cryptocurrency factors constructed in the Liu, Tsyvinski, and Wu (2022, LTW hereafter) cannot be traded at scale. At the December 2017 peak of cryptocurrency trading volume, 71% of a $100 million position in the long leg of the size factor required more than ten days of full trading volume to fill. We propose a more tradable cross section with the twenty largest coins, which together take up about 90% of the cryptocurrency market capitalization. We build a long-only mean-variance portfolio from size and momentum as expected return predictors. Separating allocation from selection with a market timing overlay lifts the after-fee Sharpe ratio above one. The resulting portfolio passes the GRS test on the seven large, long-lived cryptocurrencies, on which CAPM and the LTW model are rejected at the 1% level, and it spans the LTW factors while remaining unspanned by them.

title: Copyright Industries in the U.S. Economy: 2020 Report
affiliations: Economists Incorporated and

detail.title: Copyright Industries in the U.S. Economy: 2020 Report
detail.abstract: "Copyright Industries in the U.S. Economy: 2020 Report”, examines the contribution of copyright industries to the U.S. economy. Dr. Dutra and Dr. Stoner demonstrate that the core copyright industries of the United States provide significant value added to Gross Domestic Product (GDP), a significant number of high-paying jobs, real growth that outpaces the rest of the economy, and substantial foreign sales and exports, surpassing many industry sectors.

title: Artificial Intelligence in International Commercial Arbitration: Due Process, Disclosure, Confidentiality and the Enforceability of AI-Assisted Awards
affiliations: Senior Judicial Magistrate at Bangladesh Judicial Service

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence in International Commercial Arbitration: Due Process, Disclosure, Confidentiality and the Enforceability of AI-Assisted Awards
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is moving from the periphery of international arbitration into its ordinary working methods. Counsel use AI for research, document review, translation, chronology building and drafting; experts use it for data analysis; and tribunals increasingly confront whether, and on what conditions, AI may assist their own work. The central legal question is therefore no longer whether AI will enter international commercial arbitration, but how its use can be reconciled with the procedural legitimacy on which an arbitral award depends. This article develops a function-based framework for that inquiry. It argues that AI use should be regulated according to what the tool does, the information it receives, the degree to which its output can influence a procedural or substantive decision, and whether the use creates a material risk to a party's ability to present its case. Drawing on the New York Convention, the UNCITRAL Model Law, the 2024 SVAMC AI Guidelines, the 2025 Ciarb AI Guideline, emerging AAA-ICDR practice, the EU AI Act and UNCITRAL's 2026 work on AI in dispute resolution, the article analyses four linked issues: due process, disclosure, confidentiality and enforceability. It contends that routine, non-determinative AI assistance should not trigger a universal disclosure duty, while material adjudicative use should. It further argues that there is no free-standing 'AI ground' for refusing enforcement: an AI-assisted award should be vulnerable only where the particular use of AI translates into an established ground under the applicable arbitration law or the New York Convention. The article concludes by proposing a practical AI protocol for arbitral proceedings designed to preserve efficiency without sacrificing human responsibility, procedural equality or enforceability.

title: The Postal Rule in Modern Contract Law: Communication, Acceptance and the Challenges of Electronic Communication

detail.title: The Postal Rule in Modern Contract Law: Communication, Acceptance and the Challenges of Electronic Communication

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is based on doctrinal legal research and secondary sources, including legislation, case law, reports, and academic literature. It does not involve human participants, personal data collection, or clinical investigation. Therefore, formal ethical approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
The term “modern world” cannot be discussed without mentioning new electronic communication technologies and devices. An ordinary person in the present day cannot complete a single day without using at least one electronic device. Communication between individuals and groups largely relies on electronic devices and the internet. As we all know, communication is a fundamental aspect of contract law.
The law of contract forms the foundation of commercial law, including the law relating to sale, lease, insurance, and labour relations. Although contract law has gradually modernised over the years to accommodate changes and accepted practices, it has somewhat lagged behind the development of modern technology. Over the past 20 to 30 years, technology has developed more rapidly than anyone could have expected, creating a need for the improvement and innovation of legal rules to address the new challenges created by this technological development. However, the law has been slow to evolve in this respect, which has led to considerable ambiguity.
In all legal systems, the conclusion of a contract requires the consent or agreement of the parties, which is defined as the “manifestation of mutual assent on the part of two or more persons.”¹ Consent, however, must meet certain requirements for a contract to be effective and enforceable.
How does the law determine when a contract has been created? The universal method has been to employ the concepts of “offer” and “acceptance”. By considering the conduct of the parties, it can be determined whether an offer has been made. An offer can be described as a promise by the offeror to do, not to do, or to give something on certain conditions, leaving the option of accepting or rejecting the offer to another party, the offeree.²
At this first stage, the offeror demonstrates to the offeree his or her intention to form a contract containing certain terms between them. At this point, only the intention and wishes of one party are known.
If the offeree rejects the offer by failing to act upon it or by informing the offeror of the non-acceptance, the offer may, after a reasonable period, be considered rejected or lapsed. On the other hand, if the offeree indicates an interest in the offer and an intention to enter into a contract, this may be considered acceptance of the offer. The consent of the offeree indicates that the parties are of one mind, thereby establishing offer and acceptance and forming the contract. An offer must always be communicated to the offeree.

title: An Econometric Re-evaluation of the Impact of the Soy Moratorium on Deforestation
affiliations: Universidade Federal do Rio Grande (FURG) and Brazilian Institute for Competition and Innovation - IBCI

detail.title: An Econometric Re-evaluation of the Impact of the Soy Moratorium on Deforestation
detail.abstract: The Soy Moratorium (SM) is widely regarded as a paradigm of successful private governance in the conservation of the Brazilian Amazon. This article demonstrates that evidence of its causal efficacy becomes fragile under methodological scrutiny that isolates the impact of sectoral governance from the public policies of command-and-control implemented simultaneously. Employing Sun and Abraham's (2021) estimator for staggered treatment timing and the technique of Freyaldenhoven et al. (2021) for the adjustment of pre-event trends, the study adopts a sample selection strategy that restricts the analysis to the Amazon biome and excludes municipalities under special inspection regimes, ensuring a counterfactual based on localities with consolidated soybean production. The results indicate that SM did not produce a statistically significant marginal impact on municipal deforestation. The estimates remain statistically indistinguishable from zero across multiple specifications, including falsification tests and temporal placebos. The article concludes that the evidence supports the thesis of institutional redundancy, suggesting that private monitoring operated primarily in contexts where incentives for conservation had already been exhausted by the state apparatus.

title: The Structural Europeanisation of the European Public Sphere as a Democratic Project

detail.title: The Structural Europeanisation of the European Public Sphere as a Democratic Project

declarations.declarationOfInterest: zip
declarations.ethicsApproval: zip
declarations.funderStatement: zip

detail.abstract: This study explores the integration of advanced journalism education and digital media governance as a means to enhance the quality and reliability of news reporting within the European Public Sphere. By examining the interplay between educational initiatives and regulatory frameworks, the research aims to identify effective strategies for combating misinformation and fostering public trust in media. Through a mixed-methods approach, including qualitative interviews with media professionals and quantitative analysis of media consumption patterns, the study reveals significant correlations between education, governance, and media quality. The findings suggest that a coordinated effort in these areas can lead to a more informed citizenry and a resilient democratic environment. The primary aim of this study is to investigate how the integration of advanced journalism education and digital media governance can improve the quality of news reporting and enhance public trust in the media within the European context: 1. How does advanced journalism education influence the quality of news reporting in Europe? 2. What role does digital media governance play in mitigating misinformation and promoting transparency in news dissemination? 3. How can the combination of education and governance strategies strengthen public trust in media institutions?. The findings indicate a strong positive correlation between advanced journalism education and the perceived quality of news reporting. Respondents who reported higher levels of media literacy also expressed greater trust in media institutions. Additionally, effective digital media governance was found to significantly reduce the prevalence of misinformation, thereby enhancing the overall credibility of news sources. The study concludes that the integration of advanced journalism education and robust digital media governance is essential for improving the quality of news reporting and fostering public trust in the media. By investing in education and establishing effective regulatory frameworks, stakeholders can create a more informed citizenry and a resilient democratic environment in Europe. This coordinated approach not only addresses the challenges posed by misinformation but also strengthens the foundations of democratic participation and public discourse.

title:
Divergence of UK Law from EU Law after Brexit: 
The Example of Intellectual Property

detail.title:
Divergence of UK Law from EU Law after Brexit: 
The Example of Intellectual Property
detail.abstract: This lecture identifies and discusses five ways in which UK law has already diverged and may in future diverge from EU law, taking intellectual property law as an example. It suggests that, in a field like intellectual property law, divergence is likely to be a slow and incremental process. Moreover, it is uncertain where divergence will occur or to what extent. Where there is international agreement as to the appropriate balance between stakeholders, that may lead to the UK and the EU moving in parallel rather than diverging.

title: Projected Impacts of El-Niño on Botswana 2026

detail.title: Projected Impacts of El-Niño on Botswana 2026
detail.abstract: Botswana’s agricultural sector is at the frontline of extreme climate variability. Characterized by semi-arid conditions, rainfed agriculture and livestock remain exceptionally fragile to rainfall anomalies and extreme temperatures. As regional climate dynamics point towards an upcoming El-Niño cycle (October 2026 - March 2027), understanding the broad agricultural impacts is imperative. This report provides a quantitative stress-test of Botswana’s agricultural economy under the anticipated climate shocks. It forecasts the cascading effects of extreme temperatures and rainfall contraction across cereal crop yields and livestock.

title: Public Policies for Private Finance
affiliations: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE) - Department of Finance

detail.title: Public Policies for Private Finance
detail.abstract: We review the literature on the effectiveness of public policies to facilitate firms' access to finance. The rationale for such policies is to address market failures that cause financial constraints. Using a simple taxonomy, we discuss the current evidence on common interventions to tackle these constraints: public lending through state and development banks; public lending through private banks; subsidized credit; credit guarantee schemes; export credit agencies; publicly backed venture capital; and tax incentives for equity investors. Based on the quantity and quality of the available evidence, we summarize the policies that have proven most effective in helping firms access external financing. In addition, we highlight areas where future research is needed to address current knowledge gaps and to provide more definitive policy guidance.

title: Cross-Domain Structural Validation of HIMI: Deterministic State Classification Across Marine Telemetry, Energy Infrastructure, and Global Climate Time-Series
affiliations: Medussa Tech Research

detail.title: Cross-Domain Structural Validation of HIMI: Deterministic State Classification Across Marine Telemetry, Energy Infrastructure, and Global Climate Time-Series
detail.abstract: HIMI (Hybrid Ignition & Metabolic Indicator) is a deterministic classification engine whose parameters are fixed and identical for every caller; it maps a fixedlength time-series vector onto one of five metabolic–ignition states with no stochastic component. The first version of this paper described a cross-domain deployment as designed; this version reports it as operated. Executing the experiment required Medussa Tech Research Ltd. to consume its own HIMI API exactly as an external client would — building the ingestion layer (source fetchers, dispatch scheduling, 600-point vector construction, per-dispatch hash capture) that HIMI does not provide and every external user must supply. Standing in that external position is what exposed the discrepancies between the documented and the operated system that this version corrects, and the results are reported as a dated process record rather than a set of finished conclusions. Three domains are live. NOAA buoy signals run on eight active nodes at a ten-minute cadence — not the nine the first version projected, one declared sensor having never reported over the entire window. ENTSO-E electricity spans four regions and supplies this version’s one measured instance of temporal invariance: two genuinely different real-time cadences (fifteen and sixty minutes) drive the same fixed 600-point vector through the same engine, so within that domain HIMI is shown blind to the wall-clock span its points cover — it reads the shape of the curve, not the clock. This is the single measured toe-hold of a broader principle — that the observation window is a client parameter, not an engine parameter — which otherwise remains design principle and future work. The signals span roughly 1:4,383 in timescale, from the ten-minute buoy to the fifty-year climate series. NASA GISTEMP went live as the third domain, producing a first autonomous classification against a pre-registered, Bitcoin-anchored seed vector. The record is offered for independent audit, and the evidence for its fixedness is external to the engine. Published output hashes — vector hash sha256 over the input curve and result hash sha256 over the classification — are assembled into an RFC-6962 Merkle tree and anchored into the Bitcoin blockchain via OpenTimestamps; an outsider has reproduced the anchored root on a third machine from the public repository. Two independent registries on two hosts are shown to hold the same result set, bit for bit, over a closed window. Latency is reported as what it is: a client-side round-trip of single-digit to low-double-digit milliseconds, not an engine execution time. The limits are stated as limits. The samples are small and NASA stands at a single classification; the individual verdicts are not claimed to validate the engine. Real-time public auditability did not exist from day one — the anchored window opens after a 28 June engine correction, and the public artefact lags the live ledger. Determinism is a guarantee by construction, consistent with the reproducibility evidence but not demonstrated by a repeat-submission test, which is identified as future work. The governing discipline is to publish and timestamp inputs rather than promise re-fetch-and-compare: over twenty days, 83 of the 600 points of the live GISTEMP series were revised at the source, so the sealed vector — not the mutable source — is what a reader can trust.

title: Digital Transformation and Financial Inclusion in Kazakhstan: An Analysis of Halyk Bank's Role in Expanding Access to Financial Services

detail.title: Digital Transformation and Financial Inclusion in Kazakhstan: An Analysis of Halyk Bank's Role in Expanding Access to Financial Services

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author completed a summer internship at Halyk Finance, the brokerage subsidiary of Halyk Bank. No proprietary or confidential information was used. The author declares no financial conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable as this study relies entirely on secondary analysis of publicly available aggregated data and involves no human subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received in support of this research.

detail.abstract: Kazakhstan's banking sector has undergone a rapid digital transformation over the past decade, and Halyk Bank, the country's largest financial institution, has positioned its Super App ecosystem at the center of that shift. This paper asks a narrow question: to what extent has Halyk Bank's digital strategy contributed to financial inclusion in Kazakhstan, and what disparities remain despite that progress. Drawing on data from the World Bank Global Findex Database, the National Bank of Kazakhstan, a peer reviewed regional study, and Halyk Bank's own investor disclosures, this paper finds that digital payment adoption among Kazakhstani adults rose from 23 percent to 70 percent between 2014 and 2024, and that Halyk's share of retail deposits and loans grew alongside near total digitization of its origination process. However, a persistent nine point urban rural gap in account ownership and documented regional inequality in branch access suggest that digital growth concentrated in a single dominant bank has not, by itself, closed Kazakhstan's inclusion gap. The paper concludes that Halyk's expansion is best understood as a necessary but insufficient condition for full financial inclusion, and that regionally targeted policy, not bank level digitization alone, will determine whether the remaining gap closes.

reference: Steuer und Wirtschaft - StuW, volume 99, issue 4, 2022[10.9785/stuw-2022-990411]
title: Misperception of the Progressivity of the German Income Tax
affiliations: TRR 266 Accounting for Transparency and

detail.title: Misperception of the Progressivity of the German Income Tax

declarations.funderStatement: The authors are grateful for the funding provided by the German Research Foundation (DFG)—Collaborative Research Center (SFB/TRR), project number 403041268—TRR 266 Accounting for Transparency, for their subproject “Tax Bur-den Transparency,” from which this work originated.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Steuer und Wirtschaft - StuW, volume 99, issue 4, 2022[10.9785/stuw-2022-990411]

detail.abstract: This study shows that many people find it difficult to correctly assess the progressivity of the German income tax. The degree of the associated misperception of tax burden progressivity depends on which dimension of tax progressivity respondents are asked about. Almost half of the respondents are aware that average and marginal tax rates are increasing in income levels. Just over 23% of respondents also know that the marginal tax rate is higher than the corresponding average tax rate. However, the extent of progressivity for both tax rates is significantly underestimated, which is mainly due to the considerable overestimation of tax rates for low incomes. Knowledge of the relationship between the share of aggregate income and the contribution to total income tax revenue of the top 10% income earners is also poor. While the average estimate of this group's share of total income is surprisingly good, their contribution to total income tax revenue is dramatically underestimated, implying a regressive income tax. Regarding the progressivity of the German income tax, respondents who consider the tax contribution of the top 10% income earners to be too low demand a significant increase in progressivity. In contrast, the remaining respondents advocate a reduction of tax progressivity. Comparing the tax rates deemed fair with the actual tax rates shows that almost two thirds of the respondents believe, due to their misperception, that they are advocating for a tax cut for a gross salary of €10,000, whilst in reality their fair tax rates would lead to a tax increase.

title: Algorithmic Extortion and Digital Forgery: Deconstructing Task-based Cyber Fraud under the BNS, BSA, and IT Act
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Algorithmic Extortion and Digital Forgery: Deconstructing Task-based Cyber Fraud under the BNS, BSA, and IT Act
detail.abstract:
Modern cybercrime in India has apparently moved past the usual phishing and social engineering thing, more towards software-driven fraud and even extortion. The work-from-home task scams show this change pretty clearly, since they blend technical trickery with paperwork like contractual documents and other cues meant to feel legally legit. In this paper, we look at the technical setup, the legal framing, and the evidence side of task-based cyber fraud, and we focus on two repeat patterns you keep seeing in operations. One pattern is the use of non-judicial e-stamp papers, which are obtained in one State, then used to create a kind of illusion of contractual validity. This is then used to squeeze victims even across jurisdictional lines, as if the victim has to "agree" anyway. Another pattern is how the scheme deliberately uses server-side database errors and application lockouts, so the victim can't actually complete the assigned tasks. These patterns can involve engineered SQL primary-key collisions, or pre-scripted script failures at chosen points in the task sequence, like right near completion, and then it flips into demands for cancellation charges, penalties, or some kind of "NOC" fee.
The paper studies these acts through the lenses of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), the
Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA), the Information Technology Act, 2000, and the Indian
Contract Act, 1872. It also checks whether server logs, database entries, and network
request-response traces, when they are properly preserved and authenticated, can actually become
meaningful proof about how the fraudulent scheme was designed and run, and that in turn may help
show the required mens rea for offences like cheating under Section 318 BNS, and extortion under
Section 308 BNS. The paper further touches on the enforceability of penalty clauses in click-wrap
agreements, especially when those terms are dumped on the victim as part of a dishonest
arrangement. This is considered with reference to Section 23 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872.
A further section focuses on the evidentiary trouble with electronically generated records. It looks at
the certification conditions under Section 63 of the BSA, and it considers what the Supreme Court
clarified in Pune Bar Association v. Union of India (2026) about whether digital forensic experts can
certify the specific portion that’s relevant to the statutory certificate. On top of these legal and
technical points, and by leaning on newer ways for verification-first digital trust infrastructure, the
paper puts forward a mix of legislative, institutional, and technical reforms. These include real-time,
inter-State confirmation of e-stamp instruments, standardised Section 63 BSA evidence intake steps
for complaints received via the 1930/NCRP system, and also tools for rapid account restriction or
freezing in the early response window after a reported cyber-fraud transaction.

reference: FRB of Chicago Working Paper No. 2026-14
title: Neural Attention in Heterogeneous-Agent Economies
affiliations: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago

detail.title: Neural Attention in Heterogeneous-Agent Economies

publicationDetails.detailsText: FRB of Chicago Working Paper No. 2026-14
publicationDetails.journalName: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Transformers, the neural-network architecture behind much of modern AI, combine flexible nonlinear approximation with an attention mechanism that learns how information is combined across inputs. Can neural attention reveal which parts of an agent distribution matter for aggregate dynamics? I represent economic states as tokens—such as wealth bins, capital, debt, and productivity—and embed a transformer in a recursive Krusell–Smith-style solution method. The transformer forecasts the continuation tokenized distribution entering individual Bellman equations. Its neural-network component approximates nonlinear aggregate policy functions, while attention learns how distributional information is aggregated and yields interpretable weights. In Krusell–Smith benchmarks, the transformer rediscovers approximate aggregation, assigning nearly uniform attention across the distribution when aggregate capital is nearly sufficient. In a heterogeneous-firm economy with endogenous default, attention instead concentrates near the default margin and rises during crises for financially constrained firms when their default risk becomes more consequential for aggregate dynamics. Attention therefore serves simultaneously as a solution device and a diagnostic of economic aggregation.

title: Walter v Lane Revisited (Again)

detail.title: Walter v Lane Revisited (Again)
detail.abstract: Walter v Lane is a landmark case in UK copyright law, but one which is much misunderstood and whose status is ambiguous. This article attempts to clarify what Walter v Lane did, and did not decide, and hence its relevance to contemporary UK copyright law.

title: COSMIC SCOUT 2.0 A Falsification-Oriented Framework for Universal Complexity Detection
affiliations: Medussa Tech Research

detail.title: COSMIC SCOUT 2.0 A Falsification-Oriented Framework for Universal Complexity Detection
detail.abstract: The original Cosmic Scout framework proposed that mutation dynamics, negentropy generation, coordination structures, persistence, and evolutionary pressure may constitute domainindependent signatures of organized complexity. Such a hypothesis requires rigorous falsification. This paper introduces Cosmic Scout 2.0, a universal validation framework designed not to confirm the hypothesis, but to expose it to hostile testing environments. The protocol evaluates the framework across synthetic noise, deterministic chaos, physical systems, biological systems, social systems, technological systems, and astronomical observations. A large-scale blind classification challenge, false-positive stress testing architecture, crossdomain robustness benchmark, and adversarial validation protocol are proposed. The objective is not to detect extraterrestrial intelligence. The objective is to determine whether organized complexity leaves statistically detectable fingerprints independent of semantic context, physical substrate, or domain-specific interpretation. If successful, intelligence becomes a special case of organized complexity rather than the primary target of detection.

title: Capitalism without Prices
affiliations: Chess Ed and University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: Capitalism without Prices
detail.abstract: Beckert argues that capitalism was global from the start, that it was built by an alliance of merchants and armed states rather than by markets, and that coercion was constitutive rather than incidental. The evidence is formidable and the decentering of Europe is a real advance. The causal argument is weaker than the descriptive one. Our central claim is that the book has written a thirteen-hundred-page history of land rent without a theory of rent. Read against Ricardo, it documents capture at the extensive margin but never separates transfer from creation. Read against Henry George, it misidentifies its own defendant, since much of what it calls capitalism is landlordism, and George supplies both the mechanism and the remedy that Beckert's conclusion gropes for. Read against Veblen, it narrates the structure of pecuniary claims without the accounting system in which those claims are denominated. Read against Keynes, it has a state without expectations and crises without demand. Mises and Hayek supply the computational function of prices that the book cannot represent, and are in turn embarrassed by its evidence on how titles were made. The book also has no theory of credit, which costs it the debt contract underlying its own merchant-state alliance and the discount rate that converts rents into land values. White supplies the theory of networks that Beckert's own unit of analysis requires and lacks, and with it a price theory that fits his evidence better than the neoclassical one he declines to use. Acemoglu supplies the formal version of Beckert's own thesis and the persistence evidence that undercuts it. The residual difficulty is identification. The treatment is near universal, the sample is selected on the outcome, and the definition of capitalism is elastic enough to admit almost any case. The book is best used as an atlas, not as a proof.

title: Order-flow Provenance, Informed Entry, and Cross-venue Spreads

detail.title: Order-flow Provenance, Informed Entry, and Cross-venue Spreads
detail.abstract: Brokers route retail-labeled order flow to wholesalers, while exchanges receive the residue. We model provenance as a noisy binary classifier in a one-round, symmetric two-state Glosten-Milgrom market with endogenous informed entry. At fixed participation, the classifier lowers aggregate uninformed trading cost relative to pooling by half the value gap times the variance of the label posterior; hence Blackwell sharpening weakly raises this fixed-participation saving. With free entry, Blackwell sharpening weakly reduces informed entry and average uninformed execution costs. Its venue-level incidence is asymmetric. Every orientation-preserving sharpening lowers the retail break-even spread, whereas its effect on the exchange spread decomposes into retail- and exchange-purification margins with a closed-form threshold. Routing more uninformed flow to the retail label widens the exchange spread at every retention level below quote matching and leaves it unchanged under quote matching. Better detection of informed traders behind that label can narrow or widen it depending on the arrival-based venue mass. Greater retention reduces informed entry but raises the average uninformed-trader execution cost toward the pooled-market level. Historical and pre-amendment Rule 605 moments illustrate the model-to-data mapping and show which incidence comparisons require an external normalization or an arrival-based mass not identified by covered-volume shares.

title: Do Directors have Performers' Rights?

detail.title: Do Directors have Performers' Rights?
detail.abstract: Stage directors and film directors may be authors, and have authors' rights, but are they performers who have performers' rights? It is generally accepted that musical conductors are performers, and therefore have performers' rights. This article considers whether stage directors and film directors are performers, and whether it matters if they have performers' rights.

title: Korea’s Industrial Policy by the Numbers: A Cross-Country Comparison and Policy Implications
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: Korea’s Industrial Policy by the Numbers: A Cross-Country Comparison and Policy Implications

publicationDetails.detailsText: Korea Institute for Industrial Economics and Trade Research Paper No. 26/iKIET/220
publicationDetails.journalName: Korea Institute for Industrial Economics & Trade Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
In response to rapid shifts in the global economic and social environment, industrial policy has re-emerged as a central instrument of national strategy. Major shocks, including COVID-19, supply chain fragmentation, the AI revolution, and the green transition, have led major economies to adopt wide-ranging industrial policies at increasingly larger scales. Empirical understanding of these policies remains a blind spot in the literature, and this gap calls for systematic, quantitative, and evidence-based analysis. This study draws on the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD)'s Quantifying Industrial Strategies (QuIS) database to measure South Korea's industrial policy, and benchmark it within a group of 20 OECD economies. Industrial policy spending is rising broadly across the OECD: fiscal support climbed from 1.34 percent of GDP in 2019 to 1.55 percent in 2023. 

In Korea, however, industrial policy spending moved the other way, peaking in 2021 before declining to 1.06 percent of GDP in 2023, below the OECD benchmark. The analysis finds that Korea's industrial policy has two salient features: 1) it is typically small-scale and dispersed, and 2) predominantly horizontal. Industrial policy is spread thinly across programs, lacking concentration and heft, and is weighted heavily toward technology-oriented measures and support for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and young firms, rather than toward specific sectors. 

This contrasts with the global trend toward larger, more targeted industrial policy. The authors argue that Korea needs to expand industrial policy and make efforts to increase its effectiveness. The paper calls for debate on expanded fiscal support; shifting toward more concentrated support for core areas through clearer priorities and the consolidation of overlapping programs; stronger targeted support for advanced strategic industries alongside broader coverage that reaches beyond manufacturing into non-manufacturing and emerging sectors; and an evaluation system that looks past firm-level outcomes to ask whether policy goals such as industrial competitiveness and supply chain stability are actually met, weighing results against inputs and comparing the effectiveness of different instruments.

This paper was translated from the Korean original using the Claude Opus 5 large language model. The text was reviewed by an editor and the authorial team prior to publication.

title: Working From Home and Gendered Labour Time: COVID-19's Ongoing Impact
affiliations: University of Melbourne, University of Melbourne and

detail.title: Working From Home and Gendered Labour Time: COVID-19's Ongoing Impact

declarations.funderStatement: We acknowledge the support of Australian Research Council Grant LP190100623.

publicationDetails.journalName: Melbourne Institute of Applied Economic and Social Research Working Paper Series

detail.abstract:
The COVID-19 pandemic reshaped work arrangements, prompting widespread adoption of
working from home (WFH) and raising questions about its implications for gendered labour.
Using Australian panel data and fixed-effects models, this study investigates how WFH shapes
time allocations to paid and domestic work among dual-earner households. We examine
differential effects by gender, WFH intensity, and children’s age. Findings indicate a postpandemic
rise in WFH prevalence and intensity, accompanied by divergent gendered patterns
of labour time. Under high-intensity WFH, women particularly mothers of older children,
expanded their paid work, while men, especially fathers of young children, substantially
increased domestic work. Low-intensity WFH primarily supports additional paid work for both
women and men. Overall, the results reveal that WFH does not consistently reinforce or
challenge traditional gender patterns; rather, its effects are contingent on intensity and family
context, producing both opportunities for and constraints on gender equality in the organisation
of work.

title: Climate Dharma: Reinterpreting Bhagavad Gita for a New Global Environmental Order

detail.title: Climate Dharma: Reinterpreting Bhagavad Gita for a New Global Environmental Order
detail.abstract: This paper reinterprets a few verses from the Bhagavad Gita and uses them as a philosophical basis for climate governance. In doing so, it interprets the teachings of dharma, karma yoga, sattva, tapas, and leadership by Krishna as a normative basis for a new moral climate world order, drawing on various concepts such as climate justice and global governance. Using literature on climate justice and reports by the IPCC, the author claims that India, because of its culture and climate diplomacy, is well suited to this task.

title: AllInBench: Evaluating Strategic Reasoning in Frontier Language Models Under Imperfect Information in an Adversarial Environment (No-Limit Texas Hold'em)
affiliations: Lewis University, Bryn Mawr College, Johns Hopkins University - Whiting School of Engineering and Johns Hopkins University - Carey Business School

detail.title: AllInBench: Evaluating Strategic Reasoning in Frontier Language Models Under Imperfect Information in an Adversarial Environment (No-Limit Texas Hold'em)
detail.abstract: Which AI is the best? The field cannot agree on a scoreboard. First-generation benchmarks (static exams such as MMLU and GPQA) saturate and leak into training data, and the most-watched leaderboard measures human preference, not capability. We settle the argument the way the world settles it in soccer: with a tournament anyone can watch. AllInBench seats four frontier models (Claude Opus 5 and GPT-5.6-sol from the United States, Kimi K3 and DeepSeek V4 Pro from China) at a no-limit Texas Hold'em table under identical prompts, budgets, and rules, winner take all. Every decision is released across 84 fields, including two streams no static test can see: Table Talk, what a model says to its opponents, and Private Deliberation, what it believes. Ten games in, Claude Opus 5 leads with four wins and the United States edges China six games to four, a margin a coin flip could still explain. The text is more decisive: the models almost never lie (four deceptive statements in 148), but when they do it is engineered: deception concentrates in discretionary raises, runs in both directions, and wins pots. Each model leaves an honesty fingerprint, and even response time is a tell. A full tournament costs under $5 and ninety minutes, so the leaderboard refreshes weekly as new models ship. We release everything, and we deal again next week. Watch the live tournament at https://llm-poker-allin.vercel.app/lobby.html.

title: Human Resource Management Crisis in the Private Security Sector of Bangladesh: A Qualitative Study of Agency-employed Security Personnel in Chittagong

detail.title: Human Resource Management Crisis in the Private Security Sector of Bangladesh: A Qualitative Study of Agency-employed Security Personnel in Chittagong

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: ​The study strictly adhered to international social science research ethics guidelines (such as SAGE/BRM standards). Voluntary informed consent was obtained from all participants prior to interviews. All personal identifiers, agency affiliations, and deployment locations were fully anonymized to safeguard participants.
declarations.funderStatement: This research did not receive any specific grant or funding from public, commercial, or non-profit sector agencies. It was conducted as an independent, self-funded study.

detail.abstract:
Background & Problem: Private security guards perform vital protective functions across commercial banks, ATM booths, corporate offices, educational institutions, healthcare facilities, and residential complexes in Bangladesh. However, their statutory rights and employment conditions remain largely marginalized in scholarly literature and public policy agendas.

Methods: Adopting an interpretivist research philosophy and an inductive qualitative design, data were gathered through semi-structured interviews with 35 male security personnel (25 agency-employed guards and 10 directly employed bank guards) across diverse deployment sites in Chittagong between January and June 2026. Data saturation occurred around the 28th interview, with 35 participants finalized to ensure empirical depth.

Findings: The empirical findings reveal systemic structural HRM deficiencies within third-party staffing agencies, characterized by depressed wages, extended 10-12 hour shifts, total absence of statutory paid leave, complete career stagnation, unauthorized financial deductions by agency intermediaries, and severe lack of organizational recognition. Interpreted through Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs, Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory, Psychological Contract Theory, Human Capital Theory, and Organizational Justice Theory, these structural deficiencies engender pervasive economic precarity, acute occupational stress, emotional exhaustion, and diminished professional commitment.

Contributions: The study makes three primary contributions: (1) Theoretical: Extends organizational justice and psychological contract theories to South Asian triadic subcontracting models; (2) Empirical: Provides granular, first-hand qualitative evidence from Chittagong's commercial hub; and (3) Policy: Identifies concrete regulatory mechanisms (such as digital payroll and minimum wage indexing) to eliminate intermediary exploitation.

title: False Positives and False Negatives in Venezuelan Document Verification

detail.title: False Positives and False Negatives in Venezuelan Document Verification

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This working paper received no external funding. It was self-funded by the author through Latino Institute for Security Efficiency.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This working paper is a doctrinal and professional analysis based on the author's prosecutorial practice and forensic document examination experience. It does not involve human subjects research, patient data, or case studies requiring ethics approval.

detail.abstract: This working paper presents a taxonomy of errors documented by the author over fifteen years of prosecutorial practice in Venezuela and continued forensic examination of Venezuelan institutional documents in the U.S. immigration context. Drawing on that direct experience within the Venezuelan criminal justice system, first as a litigating attorney, then as a Prosecutor in the states of Sucre and Táchira, and later as Founder of Latino Institute for Security Efficiency, which in turn works with a network of experts in documentology, criminal investigation, and related fields, the author identifies six recurring patterns of false positives, the improper acceptance of irregular documents as genuine, and three patterns of false negatives, the unjustified rejection of authentic documents for lack of a reliable reference framework. The article quantifies the human and systemic cost of both types of error for the applicant, for the immigration system, and for the integrity of immigration justice, and lays the doctrinal groundwork for the second working paper in this series, dedicated to the corrective mechanism: expert witness testimony under Federal Rule of Evidence 702.

title: Institutionalizing Civil Society Participation in Local Planning, Budgeting, and Monitoring: Cases in Antique, Iloilo, and Misamis Oriental
affiliations: De La Salle University,  and De La Salle University

detail.title: Institutionalizing Civil Society Participation in Local Planning, Budgeting, and Monitoring: Cases in Antique, Iloilo, and Misamis Oriental

publicationDetails.detailsText: De La Salle University - Jesse M. Robredo Institute of Governance. (2017). Institutionalizing Civil Society Participation in Local Planning, Budgeting, and Monitoring: Cases in Antique, Iloilo, and Misamis Oriental. SEAOIL Foundation. Pp. 1-60.

detail.abstract:
Democratization has been moving towards a more direct and inclusive approach, with
stakeholders gaining direct access to more areas of public governance, and demanding more
results from such increase. One such area is budgeting, wherein the people, through civil society
organizations (CSOs), could plan and demand projects that would directly benefit them, most
especially the impoverished. Basing on the successes of participatory budgeting mechanisms in
Brazil and Mexico, and acknowledging the needs of the Filipino people, then-President Benigno
Aquino III and his administration introduced the Bottom-up Budgeting (BuB) Process in 2012.
By 2015, BuB has covered all of the municipalities and cities in the Philippines, each of them
having their own successes and challenges.
This paper looks at the experiences of CSOs in the BuB in four (4) selected localities in the
Philippines: Metro Iloilo, Iloilo; Tobias Fornier, Antique; Cagayan de Oro City; and Alubijid,
Misamis Oriental. The cases highlight how participation in the BuB impacted local CSOs’
quality of engagement with their respective local governments, organizational capacity, and
quality of participatory local governance. The cases also investigate how local CSOs have
optimized BuB as a space to participate in local governance.

title: Test Everything, Publish Both Results: A Protocol That Cuts Backtest False Positives from 37% to 0.4%

detail.title: Test Everything, Publish Both Results: A Protocol That Cuts Backtest False Positives from 37% to 0.4%

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests. The paper's simulations use synthetic data only; no proprietary results are reported.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper delivers four artifacts for practitioners of systematic strategy research. First, a taxonomy of recurring backtest failure modes, each with a testable diagnostic signature. Second, a Monte Carlo study of both error types across common research behaviors. Under a pure null with twenty variants per idea, tuning on the full sample falsely accepts 36.9% of candidates (a closed-form result: selecting on a reused holdout is the same quantity, since a holdout consulted for selection is not a holdout), a disciplined single holdout achieves its nominal 2.3%, and a trial-count-deflated hurdle achieves 0.4% — with the popular fold-consistency heuristic shown to be near-vacuous (87% acceptance) because selection contaminates every fold. Under an era-locked alternative — a real in-sample effect confined to one regime — the entire standard stack fails (deflation passes 95%), motivating our third artifact: leave-best-era-out (LBEO), a pre-registrable criterion that collapses era-locked acceptance to 1.2% at a null size of 0.04%, and whose measured cost is power — 7% detection of a stable SR 0.5 on eight years of dailies, versus deflation's 28%, both falling further when trial variants are realistically correlated. Severity, in other words, is purchased with power at exactly the effect sizes that survive costs, and we quantify the price rather than deny it. Fourth, the burial-record template that converts each rejection into durable research infrastructure, including an operational counting rule for the quantity deflation depends on and presentations omit: the number of trials. All results are simulation- and backtest-based; nothing here constitutes investment advice.

title:
The Magic Window: 
A Stablecoin basis between Two Bitcoin Oracles
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title:
The Magic Window: 
A Stablecoin basis between Two Bitcoin Oracles

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable: the study uses only publicly available market data and involves no human or animal subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding (self-funded).

detail.abstract:
Polymarket and Kalshi both operate hourly binary markets on the direction of Bitcoin: whether the price closes an hour higher or lower than it opened. The two venues ask the same question but settle it against different price references-Polymarket against the Binance BTC/USDT hourly candle, Kalshi against the CF Benchmarks Bitcoin Real-Time Index (BRTI), denominated in US dollars. Because these references rest on different currencies and different exchanges, they disagree by a small but persistent amount. This paper documents the structure of that disagreement, argues that it is largely a reflection of the stablecoin basis between USDT and the US dollar-and is therefore predictable before settlement-and develops a cross-venue position designed to exploit it. The position pairs two offsetting binary legs that, taken together, normally return the stake, occasionally pay double (the magic window), and, if the trade is built naively, can occasionally lose on both sides at once. We argue that this double-loss tail is not bad luck but a direct consequence of the basis, and that once the basis is accounted for in the choice of strike and direction, the tail is removed. We validate the mechanism on real settlement data; show that, at rest, the pair is fairly priced-so the only riskless edge is a sub-second latency race we do not measure, while the positive-expectation windows that do open are counted (Section 7)-and map its capacity, the execution such a strategy would require, and the conditions under which it would decay. 

On 1,350 hours of real settlement, a naive construction loses on both sides 4.6% of the time; accounting for the basis in the choice of strike and direction removes that tail entirely, to 0.0%, while lifting the double-win rate from 8.3% to 21.5%.

title: AI Techniques for Feature Extraction, Simplification and Aggregation of Geospatial Data

detail.title: AI Techniques for Feature Extraction, Simplification and Aggregation of Geospatial Data
detail.abstract: This study proposes an Artificial Intelligence (AI) application to cartographic workflow with the purpose of environmental mapping. The Random Forest (RF) framework of Machine Learning (ML) was applied to satellite image analysis for detection and robust attribution of biodiversity changes in Africa. Changes in land cover types were investigated on Landsat using comparison of several algorithms integrated in data processing and cartographic scripts using Geographic Resources Analysis Support System (GRASS) Geographic Information System (GIS). The analysis of time series highlights biodiversity changes in north Namibian landscapes in relation to presumed impacts of multiple potential environmental drivers: climate-related factors in desert setting (high fluctuations in temperature, salt crust in the saline lake and low precipitation) and anthropogenic forces (land use, abandoned areas and agriculture). The computational results demonstrated following outcomes. According to the calculated number of pixels corresponding to the cells in the raster images covering the Etosha landscapes, the land use types demonstrated the following changes: 1. Mosaic vegetation and cropland (8.42%), Aquatic or regularly flooded vegetation decreased on 13,59% due to seasonal fluctuations, areas of artificial surfaces declined insignificantly (2.40%), Mixed broadleaved deciduous forests experienced slight decreasd (1.18%), and the class of open grasslands increased to 5.32 %. Moreover, rainfed croplands demonstrated stable development with 4.58% of changes, while salt hardpans changed significantly to 12, 73%. Finally, water bodies including Etosha basin decreased significantly due to the seasonal effects (21.73%), Herbaceous vegetation, shrubland and thickets developed relatively stable with minor changes not exceeding 3.25 %, and sparse savannah grasslands occupied similar areas with fluctuations not exceeding 4,72%. The accuracy of image classification was evaluated by kappa statistics and chi-square against the ground truth data obtained from the land cover and soil data inventory. The original data with Land Use Land Cover (LULC) thematic classes were reclassified into 10 categories. The results show variations in land cover change due to arid desert climate in northern Namibia. This provides evidence of biodiversity changes in Africa detected using AI-driven data analysis using multispectral satellite images.

title: AI Revolution: The Death of Business Administration and the Birth of Inalienable Leadership

detail.title: AI Revolution: The Death of Business Administration and the Birth of Inalienable Leadership

keywords: leadership in the age of AI

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly performing administrative, analytical, coordinating, monitoring, communication, and decision-support functions historically associated with managers and business administration. This transformation does not imply the disappearance of organizations, management, managers, or business schools. It marks the erosion of administration as an exclusively human domain and as the principal justification for managerial authority. When machines can analyze, plan, coordinate, evaluate, recommend, and execute, leadership must be grounded in something deeper than superior control of information and process. Existing leadership theories explain traits, skills, behaviors, relationships, ethics, adaptation, collective agency, technological mediation, and organizational effectiveness. The documented review nevertheless identifies a higher-order question that these traditions do not make their central organizing principle: who retains final authority and responsibility over purposes, institutions, and civilizational direction when machines increasingly participate in organizational and social decision-making? This conceptual, theoretical, normative, and integrative working paper introduces and timestamps Inalienable Leadership as the first metatheory of leadership specifically formulated for the age of artificial intelligence and robotics, advances it as the overarching metatheory of leadership in that age, and formally records it as the tenth and culminating original contribution of the complete FILE contribution system. FILE (the Five Intelligences of Leadership Evolution) remains the core management theory and diagnostic framework. Inalienable Leadership integrates, grounds, governs, and gives civilizational direction to FILE and the complete FILE contribution system. The paper establishes a three-level hierarchy: Inalienable Leadership; the integrated FILE architecture (including the five meta-intelligences, the nested intelligences, the five emergent outcomes of FILE); and the distinct original contributions of the FILE Odyssey. It preserves the specific roles of Human Irreducibility, HACK, HTTPS, LENS, MAIL, MLT, and RC while placing them under one civilizational principle: humanity may share work and intelligence with machines, but it cannot surrender its final authority and responsibility for the purposes, institutions, and direction of civilization. The future will not be determined by what machines can do, but by whether humanity remains capable of leading what it creates. Humans + Machines, under human leadership.

title: SWASTH Framework: Solid Waste Action for Sustainable Towns and Habitats
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: SWASTH Framework: Solid Waste Action for Sustainable Towns and Habitats
detail.abstract: India's rapid urbanisation and consumption-driven growth have intensified municipal solid waste (MSW) generation, overwhelming existing governance mechanisms. Despite the presence of multiple regulatory instruments-such as Waste-to-Energy (WtE) initiatives, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR), and Plastic Waste Management Rulesimplementation remains fragmented, technologically mismatched, and weakly monitored. This paper proposes the SWASTH Framework (Solid Waste Action for Sustainable Towns and Habitats), an integrated policy model that aligns WtE, Plastic Neutrality, and EPR within a circular economy approach. Using secondary data analysis, policy review, and comparative case studies from Indian cities, the framework introduces decentralised organic waste processing, a traceable Plastic Credit Registry, formal integration of the informal sector, and Extended Consumer Responsibility (ECR). Implemented through a Hybrid Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model, SWASTH offers a scalable and accountable roadmap for sustainable urban waste governance in India.

title: Beyond Training Transfer: How Learning Transfer Ecosystems Transform Individual Learning into Organizational Managerial Capability

detail.title: Beyond Training Transfer: How Learning Transfer Ecosystems Transform Individual Learning into Organizational Managerial Capability
detail.abstract: Organizations invest substantially in management training with the expectation that betterinformed and more skillful managers will produce better decisions, stronger people management, improved coordination, and more adaptive execution. Yet management training does not directly create organizational managerial capability. At most, it initially produces learning located in individual managers. Whether that learning changes how an organization manages depends on a longer and more fragile process through which new practices are enacted, adapted to work realities, interpreted with others, integrated into collective action, encoded in organizational systems, and repeatedly reproduced. Training-transfer research explains many conditions affecting individual application, whereas organizational-learning and capability research explain movement across levels and the development of reliable organizational action. These literatures, however, remain insufficiently connected. This conceptual paper develops a multilevel learning transfer ecosystem framework to bridge them. A learning transfer ecosystem is defined as a dynamic and interdependent configuration of actors, relationships, work conditions, routines, technologies, and management systems that enables or constrains the application, social integration, institutionalization, and continued adaptation of learning at work. The framework specifies six linked stages: individual managerial learning; workplace application and contextual adaptation; shared interpretation and legitimation; integration into collective managerial practice; institutional encoding and recurrent enactment; and organizational managerial capability. Eight propositions explain how ecosystem coherence, opportunity-support-accountability configurations, principled adaptation, collective sensemaking, leadership sponsorship, systemic encoding, recurrent enactment, and the stability-adaptability tension shape these transitions. The paper extends training transfer beyond individual maintenance, applies organizational-learning logic to formal management development, and identifies the microfoundations through which training-derived practices may become organizational capability.

title: Anatomy of a Panic: Behavioral Biases among Indian Retail Investors During the January-April 2026 Market Drawdown

detail.title: Anatomy of a Panic: Behavioral Biases among Indian Retail Investors During the January-April 2026 Market Drawdown
detail.abstract: During the January–April 2026 drawdown in Indian equity markets, the Nifty 50 declined by roughly 16%, from an all-time high of 26,373 to a low of 22,182. Aggregate data suggested striking retail resilience: record contributions to systematic investment plans (SIPs) and net equity mutual fund inflows positive for a 61st consecutive month. This paper investigates whether individual investor behavior matched that aggregate narrative. An anonymous survey of 100 Indian retail investors (72% aged 35 or younger, 68% with under three years of market experience, 81% verified against personal transaction records) was compared against aggregate data for the identical period from the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) and the National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL). In this sample, individual behavior diverged sharply from the aggregate picture: 45% of respondents sold holdings during the decline, and contrary to the well-documented disposition effect, 64% of sellers realized losses versus only 11% realizing gains, a pattern consistent with capitulation near what proved to be a market bottom, as the index subsequently recovered roughly 10%. Herding was denied when asked directly (5–9% admission) yet evident indirectly, with 70% citing external information sources as their primary influence. Sixty-one percent rated their own decisions as “mostly rational” despite widespread reports of compelled selling and interrupted SIP contributions. The findings suggest that aggregate market resilience and individual-level panic coexisted during the drawdown, with implications for how investor education addresses acute market stress.

title: Significant Risk Transfer (SRT) as a Framework for Tokenized Real-World Assets
affiliations: City College of New York and Columbia University

detail.title: Significant Risk Transfer (SRT) as a Framework for Tokenized Real-World Assets
detail.abstract: Roughly $345 billion of real-world assets are recorded on public blockchains, and only about eight per cent of that value trades. The standard diagnoses — immature technology, regulatory uncertainty, insufficient liquidity — misidentify the constraint. This paper argues that a tokenized real-world asset is neither a security nor the underlying asset, but a synthetic risk transfer: a contract that conveys an asset’s economic exposure while legal title remains with the originator. We first set out the mechanics of both structures and show that they are the same object. We then import the analytical apparatus that the bank risk-transfer market already possesses — the supervisory assessment of whether a transfer is significant — and propose it as the organizing framework for tokenized assets. Significance, defined as the share of conveyed exposure that the originator cannot recapture, does two jobs at once: it classifies the instrument, and it prices it. We then put the apparatus to work twice more — to locate the tokenized interest in the vehicle’s capital structure, and to ask what restructuring can mean for a claim whose seniority the sponsor may alter without ever committing a default. We formalize significance, catalogue the recapture channels through which it leaks, and derive the market-structure consequences of leaving it unmeasured — adverse selection in the primary market and collateral ineligibility in the secondary.

title: The Data Paradox: Secret Prior Art and the Hidden Risk to U.S. Patents

detail.title: The Data Paradox: Secret Prior Art and the Hidden Risk to U.S. Patents

declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract: Modern data-centered inventions—including structured data architectures, training methodologies, datasets, and data-processing pipelines—are the core assets driving innovation in artificial intelligence, cloud computing, digital platforms, and emerging technologies. These inventions are typically deployed through cloud services and APIs that reveal functionality while concealing the data structures and methods that constitute the inventive contribution. Commercialization thus discloses nothing of technological value to the public. Yet under the doctrine of secret prior art—rooted in Judge Learned Hand’s Metallizing Engineering (1946) and preserved by the Supreme Court’s decision in Helsinn Healthcare v. Teva Pharmaceuticals (2019)—such confidential commercial activity can invalidate U.S. patents. This creates a hidden risk: patents may be destroyed by the very secrecy that makes data-centered inventions valuable, even though the public gains no knowledge from the commercial deployment. The risk is compounded by a global paradox. The United States stands alone among major patent jurisdictions in treating confidential commercial activity as novelty-destroying prior art. A data-centered invention invalidated in the United States may remain fully patentable under the European Patent Convention, in Japan, China, Korea, and every other WTO member country—all of which apply public accessibility as the exclusive standard for prior art. Drawing on the inclusive patent framework developed in the author’s prior work, this Article argues that public accessibility should become the sole touchstone for prior art in U.S. patent law. It traces the origins of activity-based prior art from Pennock v. Dialogue (1829) through the AIA, demonstrates that the Metallizing doctrine was designed to address problems unique to the now-abolished first-to-invent system, addresses counterarguments including monopoly-extension concerns and TRIPS obligations, and proposes both legislative and judicial reforms. Eliminating secret prior art would reduce uncertainty in U.S. patent validity, align U.S. law with international practice, and support the disclosure-driven innovation culture on which data-centered industries depend.

title: The Adaptive Intelligence Enterprise: An Architectural Model for AI‑Enabled Organisations

detail.title: The Adaptive Intelligence Enterprise: An Architectural Model for AI‑Enabled Organisations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author serves as AI Transformation Director of AI Organisational Design (In Formation, Edinburgh). AI Organisational Design operates as an emerging research and practice initiative and is not yet established as a formal legal entity.
